definition_zh: 无论如何；况且；再说
definition_en: in spite of that, or used to add a point or to change the subject
core_image: 外面下着大雨，一行人仍撑着伞出门
scene: 外面下着大雨，大家还是撑起伞出了门。 It was raining, but we went out anyway.
sceneCN: 这里 anyway 是「无论如何」（第 1 个义项：尽管有阻碍仍然如此）；句意为当时在下雨，但我们还是出门了。

senses.title: In spite of that
senses.definition: in spite of what has just been said or done
senses.definitionCN: 不顾刚才所说或所做，仍然如此
senses.example: It was raining, but we went out anyway.
senses.exampleCN: 当时在下雨，但我们还是出门了。
senses.why: Any way means by any road, so the word first says the obstacles make no difference.
senses.whyCN: any way 意为任取一条路，所以这个词首先表示阻碍不起作用。

senses.title: To add a point or change the subject
senses.definition: used to add a remark or to move to a new subject
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充一点，或转到新的话题
senses.example: Anyway, I must go now.
senses.exampleCN: 再说，我现在得走了。
senses.why: The same free road also lets the speaker turn aside and start a fresh point.
senses.whyCN: 同一条自由的路也让说话人岔开，开始一个新的话题。

intro.cn: 下面是 anyway 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Weg meant a road or a way.
items.cn: weg 意为道路或方式。

items.en: Any left the road open to every choice.
items.cn: any 让这条路向所有选择敞开。

items.en: English joined the two words as anyway.
items.cn: 英语把这两个词合成 anyway。

items.en: The joined word spread as a way to say in spite of that.
items.cn: 这个合成词作为「尽管如此」的说法传播开来。

items.en: Today it also softens a change of subject.
items.cn: 今天它也用来缓和话题的转换。

note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 any 与 way。

abstract.cn: 想象外面下着大雨，一行人仍撑着伞出门。

abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

definition_zh: 失明的；瞎的；盲目的；盲人；百叶窗；使失明
definition_en: unable to see, done without thought or reason, or to make someone unable to see
core_image: 一根白色手杖在墙边轻轻探路
scene: 一位盲人拄着白色手杖，沿着墙边慢慢向前走。 The blind man walked slowly along the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 blind 是「失明的」（第 1 个义项：看不见东西的）；句意为那位盲人沿着墙慢慢走。

pos.zh: 名词：盲人（与 the 连用）；百叶窗

collocations.zh: 相亲；由他人安排的约会

derivatives.zh: 由 blind 加 -ness 构成，义为「失明；盲目」
由 blind 加 -ly 构成，义为「盲目地；摸索地」
由 blind 与 fold 组合而成，义为「蒙住眼睛」
由 colour 与 blind 组合而成，义为「色盲的」

senses.title: Unable to see
senses.definition: not able to see, either from birth or because of illness or injury
senses.definitionCN: 看不见东西的，可能是天生，也可能因疾病或受伤
senses.example: The blind woman used a white cane.
senses.exampleCN: 那位失明的女士用一根白色手杖。
senses.why: Old English blind already meant unable to see, and that physical sense has never left the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blind 已经表示看不见，这个身体层面的义项从未离开这个词。

senses.title: Without judgement
senses.definition: done or felt without thinking clearly or judging fairly
senses.definitionCN: 未经清醒思考或公正判断就做出的、产生的
senses.example: Love can make people blind to faults.
senses.exampleCN: 爱会让人对缺点视而不见。
senses.why: A person who cannot see becomes a picture of someone who will not judge clearly, so the word moved from eyes to mind.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的人变成了不肯看清的人的比喻，于是这个词从眼睛移到心智。

senses.title: People who cannot see
senses.definition: used with the definite article to mean people who cannot see, as a group
senses.definitionCN: 与定冠词连用，作为一个群体指看不见的人
senses.example: The charity helps the blind.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构帮助盲人。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a group noun with the, and blind follows that old pattern.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 the 把形容词变成群体名词，blind 遵循的就是这个古老的模式。

senses.title: The window covering
senses.definition: a window covering made of slats that can be pulled down or tilted
senses.definitionCN: 由可放下或倾斜的板条制成的窗饰
senses.example: She closed the blinds before the sun rose.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳升起前她拉上了百叶窗。
senses.why: The covering shuts light out the way blindness shuts sight out, so the same word was given to it.
senses.whyCN: 这种窗饰把光挡在外面，正如失明把视线挡在外面，于是它得到同一个名字。

senses.title: To make unable to see
senses.definition: to make someone unable to see, often suddenly and temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 使人看不见，常指突然而短暂的
senses.example: The bright flash blinded him for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 那道强光让他一瞬间看不见了。
senses.why: The adjective became a verb: to put someone into the blind state, even if only for a second.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成了动词：把人置于失明的状态，哪怕只有一秒钟。

intro.en: Blind is a thousand-year-old English word whose physical sense later grew a figurative one.
intro.cn: blind 是有一千多年历史的英语词，身体层面的义项后来长出了比喻用法。

items.en: Old English blind already meant unable to see, and it has kept that sense for a thousand years.
items.cn: 古英语 blind 已经表示看不见，这个义项保留了一千年。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family; German blind and Dutch blind carry the same meaning.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语族，德语 blind 与荷兰语 blind 意思相同。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some scholars link it to a root for confusion or darkness.
items.cn: 更早的来源并不确定，有学者把它与表示「混乱」或「黑暗」的词根联系起来。

items.en: Middle English writers used blind for rash judgement, and that figurative sense still lives.
items.cn: 中古英语作家用 blind 指草率的判断，这个比喻义至今仍在。

items.en: The slatted window covering took the name because it shuts out light, and the verb followed later.
items.cn: 板条窗饰因为挡光而得到这个名字，动词用法则出现得更晚。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects other words about not seeing.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收其他表示「看不见」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「混合」，拼写与 blind 相近。

entries.definition: To close and open the eyes quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「眨眼」，拼写与 blind 相近。

entries.definition: Not sharp, or saying things too directly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「钝的；直率的」，拼写与 blind 相近。

entries.definition: Unable to see, used mostly in literature.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失明的」，多用于书面语。

entries.definition: Unable to see distant things clearly, or lacking foresight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「近视的；目光短浅的」。

entries.definition: Not noticing or knowing something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「没有察觉的」，对应盲目的比喻义。

normal.en: German blind and Dutch blind carry the same meaning, so the word has close relatives.

normal.en: The eyes moved to the mind: a person who will not judge is called blind too.
normal.cn: 从眼睛移到心智：不肯看清的人也被称作 blind。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with spot, date, eye and alley.
normal.cn: 它常与 spot、date、eye、alley 搭配。

normal.cn: 拼写是 b-l-i-n-d，没有不发音的字母，每个字母都要读出来。

abstract.en: See a white cane tapping along a wall: that steady tapping is blind.
abstract.cn: 想象一根白色手杖点着墙面前行：那规律的敲击声就是 blind。

abstract.en: Now shut the inner eye as well, and the word turns from eyesight to judgement.
abstract.cn: 再把心里的眼睛也闭上，这个词就从视力转向判断。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the tapping cane bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让敲墙的手杖把意思带回来。

root: blind 来自古英语 blind，一直表示「看不见」，与德语 blind、荷兰语 blind 同源。更早的词源不确定，有学者把它与表示「混乱」或「黑暗」的词根联系起来。中古英语把它从眼睛扩展到判断，指不肯看清的人；后来板条窗饰因挡光也得名，再往后又出现了「使失明」的动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of blind start from one picture: eyes that cannot see, and then anything that shuts light or judgement out.
sensesIntro.cn: blind 的五个义项都从同一个画面出发：看不见的眼睛，以及一切把光或判断挡在外面的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white cane tapping along a wall
core.cn: 核心意象：一根白色手杖沿墙点行

branches.en: THE EYES: the physical sense of not seeing is the oldest layer.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：看不见的身体义项是最古老的一层。

branches.en: THE MIND: refusal to judge clearly borrows the picture of blind eyes.
branches.cn: 心智线：不肯公正判断借用了失明双眼的画面。

branches.en: THE GROUP: with the, the adjective names people as a whole.
branches.cn: 群体线：与 the 连用，这个形容词指作为一个整体的人群。

branches.en: THE WINDOW: a covering that shuts light out takes the name of shut sight.
branches.cn: 窗饰线：把光挡在外面的窗饰，借用了「挡住视线」的名字。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the verb puts a person into the blind state.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词把人置于看不见的状态。

intro.en: Blind is a base adjective, noun and verb, so the items below are its suffixes and the words it joins.
intro.cn: blind 是基础形容词、名词兼动词，下面列出的是它的后缀以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin caecus and caecitas are recorded words for blind and blindness; they are parallels, not the source of blind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caecus 与 caecitas 分别是有记录的「瞎的」与「失明」，它们是平行词，不是 blind 的来源。

items.example: Blind is recorded in Old English.
items.exampleCN: blind 在古英语中已有记录。

definition_zh: 饥饿的；渴望的；荒年的；粗劣的
definition_en: feeling hunger, or strongly wanting something
core_image: 肚子空了，眼睛却亮了
scene: 放学铃响了很久。 The hungry children ran home as fast as they could.
sceneCN: 这里 hungry 是「饥饿的」（第 1 个义项：想吃东西的状态）；句意：饥饿的孩子们飞快地跑回家。

derivatives.zh: 饥饿地；形容词加副词后缀

senses.title: Needing food
senses.definition: feeling a need to eat
senses.definitionCN: 想吃东西的状态
senses.example: Skipping breakfast left him hungry all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 没吃早饭让他一上午都饿着。
senses.why: The adjective states the body condition directly: the stomach is empty.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接陈述身体状态：胃是空的。

senses.title: Craving something non-food
senses.definition: strongly wanting something such as knowledge or success
senses.definitionCN: 强烈想要知识或成功等事物
senses.example: The young reporter was hungry for a big story.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻记者渴望拿到大新闻。
senses.why: The stomach image is lifted to ambition: appetite without bread.
senses.whyCN: 把胃的意象抬升为抱负：没有面包的胃口。

senses.title: Marked by scarcity of food
senses.definition: describing times or places where food is scarce
senses.definitionCN: 形容食物匮乏的时期或地方
senses.example: Hungry years drove families to the cities.
senses.exampleCN: 饥馑岁月迫使家庭进城。
senses.why: A person's state is spread over years and regions: hungry winters, hungry lands.
senses.whyCN: 个人的状态铺展到年月和土地：饥饿的冬天、饥饿的土地。

senses.title: Eager and greedy
senses.definition: showing intense, almost greedy interest
senses.definitionCN: 表现出近乎贪婪的强烈兴趣
senses.example: The team gave a hungry performance in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在决赛中打得如饥似渴。
senses.why: Wanting too much becomes hunger of the eyes: desire without restraint.
senses.whyCN: 想要太多就成了眼中的饥饿：不受节制的欲望。

intro.en: Hungry is Old English hungor, hunger, plus -ig, an adjective ending. It has always been the everyday word for the state that the noun names.
intro.cn: hungry 是古英语 hungor 加形容词后缀 -ig。它一直是该名词所命名状态的日常用词。

items.en: The root *hunghuz underlies Dutch hongerig and German hungrig, the same adjective family across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 词根 *hunghuz 支撑着荷兰语 hongerig、德语 hungrig，整个日耳曼语的形容词词族同源。

items.en: Old English hungri described both empty stomachs and, early on, craving hearts.
items.cn: 古英语 hungri 既形容空胃，也很早就形容渴望的心。

items.en: Middle English hungry hardened the spelling and added hungry ground for barren land.
items.cn: 中古英语定型拼写，并用 hungry ground 指贫瘠土地。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English also used hungry of lean cattle and barren fields before the metaphor settled on people.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语也用 hungry 形容瘦畜与贫田，后来比喻才落到人身上。

items.en: Modern English kept the body sense central while hungry for became a common metaphor of ambition.
items.cn: 现代英语保持身体义为核心，hungry for 则成为雄心的常用比喻。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the hunger family and one false friend. The meaning group compares words for wanting.
note.cn: 形近组收录 hunger 词族与一个假朋友；词义组比较表示「想要」的词。

entries.definition: the noun behind this adjective; the feeling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词背后的名词；那种感觉本身。

entries.definition: in a hungry manner.
entries.definitionCN: 饥饿地。本词的副词形式。

entries.definition: feeling anger. It rhymes and ends the same way but comes from anger, not hunger.
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒的。押韵且结尾相同，但来自 anger。

entries.definition: extremely hungry, often exaggerated in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 饿极的。日常口语常作夸张用法。

entries.definition: needing water; also used metaphorically for wanting knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 口渴的。也比喻渴望知识。

entries.definition: keen and excited to do or get something, without the emptiness image.
entries.definitionCN: 热切的。积极期待，但没有空虚意象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks play on the hunger-hungry pair, the hungry for metaphor and the angry trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩在 hunger-hungry 配对、hungry for 比喻与 angry 陷阱上做文章。

normal.en: hunger plus y: the noun grows a tail and becomes the adjective.
normal.cn: hunger 加 y：名词长出尾巴变成形容词。

normal.en: go hungry means to have nothing to eat at all.
normal.cn: go hungry 指完全没饭吃。

normal.en: hungry for news: your appetite has switched from rice to headlines.
normal.cn: hungry for news：胃口从米饭换成了新闻标题。

normal.en: Do not mix hungry and angry: one is the stomach, one is the temper.
normal.cn: 别把 hungry 和 angry 弄混：一个在胃里，一个在脾气里。

normal.en: Comparatives swap y for i: hungrier, hungriest.
normal.cn: 比较级把 y 换成 i：hungrier、hungriest。

abstract.en: One image: bright eyes over an empty bowl.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：空碗上方亮着的眼睛。

abstract.en: Hunger is the simplest motivation story: emptiness pushes you toward the door.
abstract.cn: 饥饿是最简单的动机故事：空虚推你走向门。

abstract.en: Feel the two directions: food comes in, ambition pulls out.
abstract.cn: 感受两个方向：食物进来，野心向外拉。

examples.en: After the match the players were hungry and tired.
examples.cn: 比赛结束后球员们又饿又累。

examples.en: She was hungry for recognition as a writer.
examples.cn: 她渴望作为作家得到认可。

examples.en: No child should go hungry at school.
examples.cn: 在学校里不该有孩子挨饿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「慌个里」：饿得心里慌个不停，肚子咕咕作响。

root: 古英语 hungor（饥饿）加形容词后缀 -ig 构成 hungry；词根为日耳曼语 *hunghuz，与德语 hungrig 同源。词义路径为「空腹→渴望→缺粮之地」。

sensesIntro.en: Hungry states the body first, then borrows that emptiness for ambition, spreads it over barren years and lands, and finally shades into greedy eagerness.
sensesIntro.cn: hungry 先说身体，再把那份空虚借给雄心，铺到贫瘠的年月与土地，最后淡入近乎贪婪的热切。

core.en: An empty stomach turned into a describing word, then lent to every kind of wanting.
core.cn: 把空胃变成一个描述词，再借给一切形式的想要。

branches.en: BODY STATE: the everyday word for needing a meal.
branches.cn: 身体状态：日常说该吃饭了的那句话。

branches.en: AMBITION: hungry for success, knowledge or news.
branches.cn: 雄心：hungry for 成功、知识或新闻。

branches.en: SCARCE LAND: hungry years and hungry soil.
branches.cn: 匮乏之地：饥饿的年月与贫瘠的土壤。

branches.en: GREED: hungry eyes that want more than they need.
branches.cn: 贪婪：想要超出所需的 hungry eyes。

branches.en: SURVIVAL: go hungry, when want becomes a real risk.
branches.cn: 生存：go hungry，匮乏变成实际危险。

intro.en: Hungry shows the common adjective ending -y attached to a noun; its family adds hungrily, hungrier and the compound half-hungry.
intro.cn: hungry 展示了名词加形容词后缀 -y 的常见构词；词族还有 hungrily、hungrier 及复合词 half-hungry。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空；这是纯日耳曼语的形容词词族。

Many families went hungry that winter.

definition_zh: 出声地；大声地；朗读地

core_image: 学生在教室里朗读课文
scene: 教室里，一名学生站起来朗读课文。 Please read the sentence aloud.

pos.zh: 副词：出声地；大声地；朗读地

senses.title: With a voice others hear
senses.definition: in a voice that can be heard, not silently
senses.definitionCN: 用别人能听见的声音，而不是默读
senses.example: Please read the sentence aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 请把这个句子读出声。
senses.why: A- plus loud first meant in a loud voice, so the word marks sound that leaves the mouth.
senses.whyCN: a- 加 loud 本义是「用响亮的声音」，所以这个词标记从嘴里发出的声音。

senses.title: At a strong volume
senses.definition: in a strong, raised voice
senses.definitionCN: 用响亮、提高的音量

senses.exampleCN: 他在黑暗中大声呼叫。
senses.why: The same picture pushed to a higher volume gives the sense of calling loudly.
senses.whyCN: 同一个画面把音量推高，就得到大声呼叫的意思。

intro.en: The recorded history of aloud is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 aloud 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old phrase meant in a loud voice, with on and hlud.
items.cn: 古短语意为用响亮的声音，由 on 与 hlud 构成。

items.en: Middle English joined the phrase into one word.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个短语合成一个词。

items.en: English used aloud for speaking that others could hear.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 aloud 指别人能听见的说话。

items.en: Schools later used it for reading a text out in class.
items.cn: 后来学校用它指在课堂上把课文读出来。

items.en: Today it often stands beside read, think and speak.
items.cn: 今天它常与 read、think、speak 搭配。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The adverb for making a strong sound.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指大声地。

entries.definition: It sounds the same but means permitted.

entries.definition: It stresses that words can be understood.

normal.en: a- means on and loud means a strong sound: aloud is with a voice that can be heard.

normal.en: The same family also gives loud and loudly.

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase read aloud.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「朗读」这个搭配里。

normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 aloud 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: in a voice that can be heard, not silently.

definition_zh: 童年；幼年时代；童年时期
definition_en: the time in life when someone is a child
core_image: 人生最初的一段路，铺满玩具和欢笑
scene: 整理旧书柜时，一张小小的照片从相册里滑落出来。 This photo brings back my childhood.
sceneCN: 这里 childhood 是「童年时期」（第 1 个义项：人生中还是孩子的阶段）；句意是这张照片勾起了我的童年回忆。

derivatives.zh: childhood 的基础词，义为「小孩；儿童」
由 adult 加后缀 -hood 构成，义为「成年时期」

senses.title: The period of being a child
senses.definition: the state or time of being a child
senses.definitionCN: 人生中作为孩子的阶段
senses.example: He spent his childhood in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一个小镇上度过了童年。
senses.why: The suffix -hood turns 'child' into the time and state of being one.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -hood 把「孩子」变成「作为孩子的那段时光和状态」。

senses.title: The early period of something
senses.definition: the early period in the development of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物发展的最初阶段
senses.example: The museum was still in its childhood then.
senses.exampleCN: 那时博物馆还处于初创阶段。
senses.why: Growing organizations are compared to growing children.
senses.whyCN: 成长中的机构被比作成长中的孩子，义项由此而来。

intro.en: Childhood is simply child plus an old suffix for states of being.
intro.cn: childhood 就是 child 加上一个表示「状态」的古老后缀。

items.en: Old English cild meant a young person, the base of the whole family.
items.cn: 古英语 cild 指年轻人，是整个词族的基础。

items.en: Old English -had was a suffix meaning state, rank or manner.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -had 表示状态、身份或方式。

items.en: Middle English reshaped the suffix as -hede, -hode and finally -hood.
items.cn: 中古英语把后缀演变为 -hede、-hode，最终定型为 -hood。

items.en: Middle English formed childhede and childhod for the time of being a child.
items.cn: 中古英语据此造出 childhede、childhod，指做孩子的时光。

items.en: Modern English settled the spelling as childhood, common since the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 现代英语定型拼写为 childhood，十七世纪起已很常用。

note.en: The first group shows the family built with -hood; the second shows words for life stages.
note.cn: 第一组展示用 -hood 构成的同族词，第二组收人生阶段的词。

normal.en: a happy childhood is often mentioned in stories.

abstract.cn: 想象一条路，最初一英里散落着玩具。

abstract.en: Hear laughter echoing from a playground long ago.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见很久以前操场上的笑声回荡。

abstract.en: Feel the warmth of looking at an old photo album.
abstract.cn: 感受翻看旧相册时的那阵暖意。

examples.cn: 我的童年满是户外游戏。

examples.cn: 这座小镇已度过初创期，成长为繁忙的港口。

definition_zh: 饥饿；渴望；胃口；饥荒
definition_en: the feeling of needing food, or a strong desire for something
core_image: 空胃在喊叫，或心在向某物伸手
scene: 救援物资迟迟未到。 The refugees were weak with hunger after days of walking.
sceneCN: 这里 hunger 是「饥饿」（第 1 个义项：缺少食物的状态）；句意：难民走了几天之后饿得虚弱无力。

derivatives.zh: 饥饿的；由名词变形容词后缀而来

senses.title: The need for food
senses.definition: the uncomfortable feeling caused by lack of food
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少食物而产生的不适感
senses.example: Hunger drove them to eat wild fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 饥饿驱使他们吃野果。
senses.why: The core bodily image is an empty stomach demanding to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 核心的身体意象是空胃在要求被填满。

senses.title: Strong desire for something
senses.definition: a very strong wish for something non-physical
senses.definitionCN: 对非物质事物的强烈愿望
senses.example: Her hunger for success never faded.
senses.exampleCN: 她对成功的渴望从未消退。
senses.why: The stomach ache is mapped onto the heart: wanting something feels like wanting food.
senses.whyCN: 胃的空虚被映射到心上：渴望某物如同渴望食物。

senses.title: Widespread shortage of food
senses.definition: a period when many people in an area do not have enough food
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区许多人吃不饱的时期
senses.example: The war brought hunger to the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 战争使整个地区陷入饥荒。
senses.why: One person's empty stomach scaled up to a whole population becomes famine.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的空胃放大到全体人群，就成了饥荒。

senses.title: To hunger for: to crave
senses.definition: to have a strong desire for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物怀有强烈渴望
senses.example: They hungered for news of home.
senses.exampleCN: 他们渴盼家乡的消息。
senses.why: The noun is turned into a verb: to feel that stomach-like pull toward something.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：像胃那样朝某物拉扯。

intro.en: Hunger comes from Old English hungor, from a Germanic root shared with hungry, the same root that gives Latin fames its cousin in other families. It has always joined the body and the heart.
intro.cn: hunger 来自古英语 hungor，出自与 hungry 同源的日耳曼词根，始终同时连着身体与心灵。

items.en: The reconstructed root *hunghuz meant to hunger; cognates appear in Dutch honger and German Hunger.
items.cn: 重构词根 *hunghuz 意为饥饿，同源词见于荷兰语 honger、德语 Hunger。

items.en: Old English hungor named both famine and appetite; the verb hungrian meant to hunger for.
items.cn: 古英语 hungor 兼指饥荒与食欲，动词 hungrian 意为渴求。

items.en: Middle English hunger kept the food sense and grew the desire sense in religious writing about hungering for righteousness.
items.cn: 中古英语保留食物义，并在宗教文本「渴慕公义」中长出渴望义。

items.en: Early modern English favored hunger as a verb of craving in sermons and poetry.
items.cn: 近代早期英语在布道文与诗歌中偏爱把 hunger 用作渴求动词。

items.en: Modern English added hunger strike in the nineteenth century, when refusing food became a political weapon.
items.cn: 现代英语在十九世纪加入 hunger strike，绝食成为政治抗争手段。

normal.en: hunger for knowledge: your stomach-style ache is now aimed at facts.
normal.cn: hunger for knowledge：胃式的空虚转向了知识。

normal.en: hunger strike is refusing food on purpose; the word is used as a weapon.
normal.cn: hunger strike 是主动拒食，这个词被当作武器使用。

normal.en: die of hunger is the strongest fixed phrase; famine is the public-scale version.
normal.cn: die of hunger 是最重的固定说法；famine 是它的公共规模版本。

normal.en: Remember the pair: hunger is the feeling, hungry is the state.
normal.cn: 记住配对：hunger 是那种感觉，hungry 是那种状态。

abstract.en: One image: a bell inside the body rings until it is fed, by bread or by a dream.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：体内的钟一直响，直到被面包或被梦想喂饱。

abstract.en: Wanting is physical first; every mental desire borrows the stomach's language.
abstract.cn: 欲望先是身体的，一切心理渴望都借用了胃的语言。

abstract.en: Scale matters: one belly, one heart, one whole region starving.
abstract.cn: 尺度很重要：一副肠胃、一颗心、一整片挨饿的地区。

examples.en: He collapsed from hunger after three days.
examples.cn: 三天后他饿倒了。

examples.en: The child showed a real hunger to learn.
examples.cn: 这孩子表现出真正的求知渴望。

examples.en: Millions faced hunger that winter.
examples.cn: 那年冬天数百万人面临饥饿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「慌戈」：饿得发慌，拿着戈到处找吃的。

root: 古英语 hungor「饥饿」，出自日耳曼语词根 *hunghuz，与德语 Hunger、荷兰语 honger 同源；词义路径为「胃的空虚→心灵的渴望→全地区的饥荒」。

sensesIntro.en: Hunger starts in the stomach, climbs into the heart as desire for anything, widens to a region without food, and turns back into a verb for craving.
sensesIntro.cn: hunger 从胃出发，升入心中成为对一切的渴望，扩展为整片无粮之地，再折回动词表示渴求。

core.en: An emptiness inside that demands to be filled, with food or with anything.
core.cn: 内在的空虚要求被填满，用食物或用任何东西。

branches.en: BODY: the physical need for food.
branches.cn: 身体：对食物的生理需要。

branches.en: HEART: desire aimed at success, knowledge or love.
branches.cn: 心灵：指向成功、知识或爱的渴望。

branches.en: REGION: famine, hunger at the scale of a population.
branches.cn: 地区：饥荒，整个群体的饥饿。

branches.en: VERB: hungering for, the pull phrased as an action.
branches.cn: 动词：hungering for，把拉扯说成动作。

branches.en: WEAPON: the hunger strike, refusing the body's need to make a point.
branches.cn: 武器：绝食抗议，用拒绝对身体需求的满足来表达诉求。

intro.en: Hunger is a bare Germanic noun; the family adds hungry, hungered and compounds like hunger strike.
intro.cn: hunger 是光杆日耳曼名词；词族加了 hungry、hungered 及 hunger strike 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty because this word family is purely Germanic; appetite and famine come from Latin but are not related.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空，因为本词族纯出日耳曼语；appetite 与 famine 来自拉丁语但无亲缘。

items.meaning: the need for food; strong desire

items.example: The hungry child rubbed his eyes.
The prisoners began a hunger strike.
His hungers drove him from city to city.
items.exampleCN: 种种渴望驱使他辗转各城。
这种药使病人没有饥饿感。

items.example: She looked hungeringly at the display.

definition_zh: 表达；表示；榨出；特快的；快递；明确的
definition_en: to say or show what you think or feel, or to press liquid out of something
core_image: 手一压，汁水从果子里出来，话从心里出来，两件事是同一个动作
scene: 早餐店里，店主把刚榨好的橙汁递给客人，说： We express the oranges fresh every morning.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「榨出、压出汁液」（第 3 个义项：用压力把汁液挤出）；句意为这家店每天早上现榨橙子。

senses.title: Say what one thinks or feels
senses.titleCN: 说出自己的想法或感受
senses.definition: to put thoughts or feelings into words
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或感受用词语说出来
senses.example: He expressed his doubts politely but clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有礼而清楚地表达了自己的疑虑。
senses.why: The oldest image is pressing something out, and a thought pressed out through the mouth becomes speech.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是把东西压出来，而想法从嘴里被压出就成了言语。

senses.title: Show feeling through art or action
senses.titleCN: 通过艺术或行为表现情感
senses.definition: to show a feeling or idea through a work, gesture or act rather than a statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过作品、姿态或行为而不是陈述来显示情感或观点
senses.example: The mural expresses the community's grief.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画表达了社区的悲伤。
senses.why: The channel need not be words; anything that lets an inner state come out can carry the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 渠道不必是词语；任何能让内在状态出来的东西都能承载同一个动词。

senses.title: Press juice or oil out
senses.definition: to squeeze liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用压力从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体
senses.example: The press expresses oil from the seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子里榨出油。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning, still alive in food processing and perfumery.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面意义，在食品加工与香料制作中仍然活着。

senses.title: A fast train
senses.definition: a train that makes few stops and travels quickly
senses.definitionCN: 停站少、运行速度快的列车
senses.example: They caught the night express to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搭上了开往海岸的夜间特快。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century railways borrowed the word to mean a service that presses straight through without delays.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的铁路借用这个词，指一路直推、不作耽搁的服务。

senses.title: Fast delivery service
senses.definition: a service that sends letters or parcels quickly and directly
senses.definitionCN: 快速直接地寄送信件或包裹的服务
senses.example: The package went by express and arrived next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹走快递，第二天早上就到了。
senses.why: The same idea of direct speed moved from trains to mail and parcels.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「直达速度」从列车移到了邮件与包裹。

senses.title: Clearly stated and deliberate
senses.titleCN: 明确说出的；特意如此的
senses.definition: stated openly and with a clear purpose, rather than implied
senses.definitionCN: 公开说明且目的清楚，而非暗示的
senses.example: She came with the express purpose of resigning.
senses.exampleCN: 她来的明确目的就是辞职。
senses.why: Something expressly set out is pressed into clear view, so the adjective came to mean explicit.
senses.whyCN: 被明确摆出来的东西是被压进清晰视野的，因此这个形容词引申为「明确的」。

senses.title: Represent by symbols
senses.definition: to represent a value, relation or idea in symbols or a formula
senses.definitionCN: 用符号或公式表示一个值、关系或观点
senses.example: Express the ratio as a fraction in lowest terms.
senses.exampleCN: 把这个比表示成最简分数。
senses.why: Mathematics presses an abstract relation into visible symbols, continuing the same outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 数学把抽象关系压进可见符号，延续同一个向外的动作。

senses.title: Cause a gene to produce a product
senses.definition: in biology, to make the information in a gene produce a working molecule
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，使基因中的信息产生可用的分子
senses.example: These cells express the protein at high levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞高水平地表达这种蛋白质。
senses.why: A gene's instructions are pressed out into the cell as a product, which is why the same verb serves biology.
senses.whyCN: 基因的指令被压出到细胞里成为产物，因此同一个动词也服务于生物学。

intro.en: Express comes through Old French from Latin exprimere 'to press out, represent', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: express 经古法语来自拉丁语 exprimere「压出、表现」，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere 'to press' is the physical core. Its deeper origin is not established, and the root form often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere「压」是物理核心。其更深来源未得到证明，常为它提出的词根形式属于重构。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere gave exprimere 'to squeeze out'; the verb then acquired the mental sense 'to represent, portray, utter'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 得到 exprimere「挤出」；这个动词随后获得「表现、描绘、说出」的心理意义。

items.en: Old French espresser and expresser carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century with both the physical and the representational senses.
items.cn: 古法语 espresser 与 expresser 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，同时带有物理义与表现义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century a special messenger or dispatch was called an express; railways extended the label to fast trains in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，专门的信使或急件被称为 express；铁路在十九世纪把这个标签扩展到快车。

items.en: The adjective meaning 'clearly stated' developed in the sixteenth century from the idea of something expressly set out.
items.cn: 表示「明确说出」的形容词义在十六世纪发展出来，来自「被特意摆出来」的想法。

items.en: Source uncertain: exact dates of the railway and mail senses vary by region, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：铁路义与邮件义的确切年代因地区而异，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same or neighbouring roots; group two holds near synonyms for the core act of saying or showing.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根或邻近词根的外形相近词；第二组是「说」与「显示」这一核心动作的近义词。

entries.definition: Italian borrowed the same Latin verb for coffee pressed out under steam, so the coffee and the English verb share a root.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语借用了同一个拉丁动词，指用蒸汽压出的咖啡，因此这种咖啡与英语动词同根。

entries.definition: With 'in' rather than 'out': to press a mark or feeling into someone's mind rather than to bring something out.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：把印记或感受压进某人心里，而不是把东西带出来。

entries.definition: It looks like a sibling, but its root means 'to drive', not 'to press'; it means to force someone or something out.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像同族词，其实词根意为「驱赶」而非「压」；意思是把某人或某物赶出去。

entries.definition: It shares the 'out' prefix but its root means 'to draw or pull'; extraction pulls something out rather than pressing it.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带「向外」前缀，但词根意为「拉、抽」；提取是拉出某物，而不是压出。

entries.definition: To carry an idea across to someone; it stresses successful transfer, while express stresses the outward act.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法传递给别人；强调成功送达，而 express 强调向外的动作。

entries.definition: To say something clearly and formally; express is broader and can cover art, gestures and formulas.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而正式地说出；express 更宽，可涵盖艺术、姿态与公式。

entries.definition: A formal verb for producing sounds or words; it has no physical squeezing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指发出声音或词语的正式动词；没有物理上的挤压义。

entries.definition: To express an idea clearly and in an organized way; it adds the idea of clear structure.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而有条理地表达想法；多出「结构清晰」这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing image, the prefix contrast, the transport sense and the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：压出意象、前缀对比、交通义与同族词。

normal.en: The root means 'press out': juice is expressed from fruit, words from a mind.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压出」：从果子里压出汁，从心里压出话。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing is express, inward pressing is impress.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压是「表达」，向内压是「给人印象」。

normal.en: Transport pair: an express train and express mail both move directly and quickly.
normal.cn: 交通配对：特快列车与快递都直达而迅速。

normal.en: The adjective with purpose means explicit, as in an express purpose.
normal.cn: 与「目的」一词连用的形容词义表示「明确的」，如明确目的。

normal.en: The family runs express, expression, expressive and expressly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括动词、名词、形容词与副词四种形式。

abstract.en: Picture an orange and a sentence both being squeezed by the same hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙子和一句话被同一只手挤压。

abstract.en: Picture a train that never stops until it reaches the coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车一路不停，直到抵达海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a thought packed into a parcel and sent overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法被装进包裹，连夜寄出。

examples.en: She expressed her thanks with a small hand-written note.
examples.cn: 她用一张手写的小纸条表达了感谢。

examples.en: The factory expresses oil from locally grown seeds.
examples.cn: 这家工厂用当地种植的种子榨油。

examples.en: The express leaves the city at six and reaches the border by noon.
examples.cn: 特快列车六点离城，中午前到达边境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外压」——把话压出来是说，把汁压出来是榨 → 表达、榨出

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」；premere 更深来源不确定，相关词根形式为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pressure: words out of a mind, feeling out through art, juice out of fruit, speed out of a schedule, clarity out of a statement, symbols out of a relation and a product out of a gene.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一股压力展开：从心里压出话语、通过艺术压出情感、从果子压出汁液、从时刻表压出速度、从陈述压出明确、从关系压出符号、从基因压出产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand presses, and what was inside comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：手一压，里面的东西就出来了。

branches.en: SAY AND SHOW: words and art are two outlets for the same inner pressure.
branches.cn: 说与显：词语与艺术是同一股内在压力的两个出口。

branches.en: LIQUID OUT: the literal squeeze that keeps the root meaning alive.
branches.cn: 汁液出来：字面上的挤压，让词根意义继续活着。

branches.en: DIRECT SPEED: a train and a parcel service both press straight through without delay.
branches.cn: 直达速度：列车与包裹服务都一路直推、不作耽搁。

branches.en: PRESSED INTO CLARITY: something expressly set out cannot be mistaken for an implication.
branches.cn: 压成清晰：特意摆出来的东西不会被误当成暗示。

branches.en: SYMBOL AND CELL: a formula and a gene both make an inner relation or instruction visible and active.
branches.cn: 符号与细胞：公式与基因都让内在关系或指令变得可见并发挥作用。

intro.en: Express is a Latin verb of pressing, and its parts also build nouns, adjectives and adverbs for showing and squeezing.
intro.cn: express 是一个表示「压」的拉丁动词，其部件还构成表示「表现」与「挤压」的名词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- 'out' and premere 'to press' form exprimere; the noun expressio and the adjective expressus extend the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成 exprimere；名词 expressio 与形容词 expressus 延续同一词族。

items.example: The prefix sends the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作送向外面。

items.example: The root names the force behind the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名动作背后的力量。

items.meaning: to press out; to say or show
items.example: The press expresses oil from the seeds.
items.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子里榨出油。

items.example: The letter was warm and expressive.
items.exampleCN: 这封信温暖而富有表现力。

items.example: The rules expressly forbid the practice.
items.exampleCN: 规则明确禁止这种做法。

items.structure: Italian espresso, from the same Latin verb
items.example: The barista pulled a short espresso.
items.exampleCN: 咖啡师压出一小杯浓缩咖啡。

items.meaning: to press a mark or feeling in
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲给听众留下了深刻印象。

definition_zh: 壳；炮弹；剥壳；炮击
definition_en: a hard outer case, an explosive projectile, to remove such a case, or to attack with shells
core_image: 一只海螺壳贴在耳边，里面传出海的声音
scene: 她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。 She found a shell on the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 shell 是「壳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。

senses.title: Hard case
senses.definition: the hard outer covering of an egg, nut, or sea creature
senses.definitionCN: 蛋、坚果或海洋生物的坚硬外壳
senses.example: She found a shell on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。
senses.why: This is the basic natural sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的自然义项。

senses.title: Projectile
senses.definition: a metal case filled with explosive fired from a gun
senses.definitionCN: 从火炮发射的装填炸药的金属弹体
senses.example: An old shell was found in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 田里发现了一枚旧炮弹。
senses.why: A metal case protects what is inside, as a shell does.
senses.whyCN: 金属外壳像壳一样保护内部。

senses.title: Remove the case
senses.definition: to remove the shell from nuts or seafood
senses.definitionCN: 去掉坚果或海鲜的壳
senses.example: They shelled the peas.
senses.exampleCN: 他们剥了豌豆。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of removing a case.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为去壳的动词。

senses.title: Bombard
senses.definition: to attack a place with explosive shells
senses.definitionCN: 用爆炸弹体攻击某地
senses.example: The town was shelled for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上被炮击了数小时。
senses.why: The projectile became the action of firing it.
senses.whyCN: 弹体转化为发射它的动作。

intro.en: Shell comes from Old English scell, a hard outer covering.
intro.cn: shell 源自古英语 scell，意为坚硬的外壳。

items.en: The root named a hard covering.
items.cn: 这个词根指坚硬的覆盖物。

items.en: Scell meant the shell of an egg or nut.
items.cn: scell 指蛋壳或坚果壳。

items.en: Shell named the case of sea creatures.
items.cn: shell 指海洋生物的外壳。

items.en: Shell named an explosive projectile.
items.cn: shell 指爆炸性弹体。

items.en: The verb meant to remove a shell or to bombard.
items.cn: 动词形式意为去壳或炮击。

note.en: Shell is compared with similar-looking words and with words for coverings.
note.cn: 把 shell 与形近词以及表示外壳的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flat board for storage
entries.definitionCN: 搁板

entries.definition: a farm animal with wool
entries.definitionCN: 绵羊

entries.definition: used for future or offers
entries.definitionCN: 将要

entries.definitionCN: 外壳

entries.definition: the dry cover of grain

entries.definitionCN: 装甲

normalIntro.en: Shell is a hard outside that protects a soft inside, from eggs to warships.
normalIntro.cn: shell 是保护柔软内部的坚硬外层，从鸡蛋到军舰都一样。

normal.en: The egg shell cracked.
normal.cn: 蛋壳裂了。

normal.en: She collects sea shells.
normal.cn: 她收集贝壳。

normal.en: They shelled the nuts.
normal.cn: 他们剥了坚果。

normal.en: The building was shelled.
normal.cn: 这栋建筑被炮击。

normal.en: The turtle pulled into its shell.
normal.cn: 乌龟缩进壳里。

abstract.en: A shell is a boundary that can be left behind.
abstract.cn: 壳是可以被留下的边界。

abstract.en: Protection and weapon share one word.
abstract.cn: 保护与武器共用一个词。

abstract.en: What is empty inside is still a shell.
abstract.cn: 里面空了，仍然是个壳。

examples.en: She found a shell on the beach.
examples.cn: 她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。

examples.en: They shelled the peas.
examples.cn: 他们剥了豌豆。

examples.en: The town was shelled for hours.
examples.cn: 镇上被炮击了数小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: shell 源自古英语 scell（硬壳），核心义「包住内部的硬外层」，由蛋壳、贝壳引申为弹壳与炮击。

root: 源自古英语 scell（硬壳），核心义「保护内部的坚硬外层」。

sensesIntro.en: Shell means a hard case, a projectile, to remove a case, or to bombard.
sensesIntro.cn: shell 意为硬壳、炮弹、剥壳或炮击。

core.en: A hard outside around a softer inside.
core.cn: 包住柔软内部的坚硬外层。

branches.en: A natural hard covering.
branches.cn: 天然的硬壳。

branches.en: A metal case filled with explosive.
branches.cn: 装炸药的金属弹壳。

branches.en: The act of taking a shell off.
branches.cn: 去掉壳的动作。

branches.en: The act of firing shells.
branches.cn: 发射炮弹的动作。

branches.en: The case and the attack share one word.
branches.cn: 弹壳与炮击共用一个词。

intro.en: Shell builds words for animals, weapons, and protection.
intro.cn: shell 构成表示动物、武器和防护的词。

latinIntro.en: Shell has no Latin ancestor; Latin testa, a shell, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shell 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 testa（壳）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: bombarded or removed from a shell
items.example: Shelled nuts are easier to eat.

items.meaning: a sea animal with a shell
the hard case of a nut
items.example: In a nutshell, the plan works.

definition_zh: 借出；借给；增添（色彩等）
definition_en: to give something to someone for a short time, expecting it back; to add a quality to something
core_image: 手伸出去，东西暂时离开你的手
scene: 同学忘了带笔，他从笔袋里抽出一支递过去。 Can you lend me your umbrella for an hour?
sceneCN: 这里 lend 是「暂时给出、期待归还」（第 1 个义项：借出）；句意为能否把伞借我一小时。

derivatives.zh: lend 加施事后缀 -er，指「出借人；放贷者」
与 lend 同族（斯堪的纳维亚词源），指「贷款；借出物」

senses.title: To give temporarily, expecting return
senses.definition: to give something to someone for a time, expecting it back
senses.definitionCN: 把某物给某人一段时间，期待归还
senses.example: Can you lend me your umbrella for an hour?
senses.exampleCN: 能把伞借我一小时吗？
senses.why: The core image is a hand stretched out with a return ticket attached.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只伸出去的手，附带着归还的凭据。

senses.title: To provide money at interest
senses.definition: to give money to someone who will pay it back, often with interest
senses.definitionCN: 把钱给将偿还的人，常收利息
senses.example: The bank lends to small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 银行向小企业放贷。
senses.why: Money is just the returnable thing, so lending cash is the same motion with interest attached.
senses.whyCN: 钱不过是可归还之物，放贷就是同一动作附加利息。

senses.title: To add a quality
senses.definition: to give a quality or impression to something
senses.definitionCN: 给某物增添一种品质或印象
senses.example: The sunset lent warmth to the street.
senses.exampleCN: 落日给街道添了暖意。
senses.why: Qualities can be handed over like objects, so the concrete verb stretches to the abstract.
senses.whyCN: 品质可以像物件一样「递」，于是具体动词延伸到抽象。

senses.title: To offer help or attention
senses.definition: to offer a hand, an ear, or support
senses.definitionCN: 提供援手、倾听或支持
senses.example: He lent a hand with the boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 他帮忙搬了箱子。
senses.why: A hand or an ear is lent out and taken back, matching the temporary-giving idea.
senses.whyCN: 援手与耳朵也能「借出归还」，与暂时给出之意吻合。

senses.title: To contribute a role or suitability
senses.definition: to make something suitable for a purpose, as in lend itself to
senses.definitionCN: 使某物适合某用途，如 lend itself to
senses.example: The room lends itself to quiet study.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子适合安静学习。
senses.why: The room hands its features to the activity, as if offering itself on loan.
senses.whyCN: 屋子把自身特质「递」给活动，仿佛把自己出借。

intro.en: Lend comes from Old English laenan "to lend", from Germanic laihiwnjan, related to a root meaning "to let, permit"; loan is a Norse cousin of the same family.
intro.cn: lend 来自古英语 laenan「借出」，出自日耳曼语 laihiwnjan，与意为「允许」的词根相关；loan 是同族的诺斯表亲。

items.en: Old English laenan meant 'to lend', built on a verb meaning 'to let someone have'.
items.cn: 古英语 laenan 意为「借出」，建立在「让某人拥有」的动词之上。

items.en: Germanic laihiwnjan shows the -jan causative ending: to cause someone to have something.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 laihiwnjan 带使役后缀 -jan：使某人拥有某物。

items.en: Norse loan and related laan reinforced the family; English took loan from Norse while keeping lend native.
items.cn: 诺斯语的 loan 及相关形式巩固了词族；英语从诺斯语取 loan，而保留本族的 lend。

items.en: In Middle English lend spread to money-lending as commerce grew.
items.cn: 中古英语随商业发展把 lend 扩展到资金借贷。

items.en: Modern English added the abstract sense of lending qualities, hands and ears.
items.cn: 现代英语新增了借出品质、援手与耳朵的抽象义。

note.en: Group one flags look-alikes; group two lists the give-and-take family.
note.cn: 第一组标出形近词；第二组列出给取词族。

entries.definition: Earth as opposed to sea; one vowel apart, unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 陆地；仅差一个元音，词根无关。

entries.definition: The past tense of lend; also the church season with capital L.
entries.definitionCN: lend 的过去式；大写 L 也是教会节期。

entries.definition: One who lends, especially money.
entries.definitionCN: 出借者，尤指放贷者。

entries.definition: The noun for the thing lent, or the act; American English also uses loan as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 借出物或行为的名词；美式英语也用 loan 作动词。

entries.definition: To take temporarily; lend is the giving side of the same exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时取用；lend 是同一交换中给出的一侧。

entries.definition: To hand over permanently; lend expects the thing back.
entries.definitionCN: 永久交出；lend 期待归还。

entries.definition: To give formally, often rights or money.
entries.definitionCN: 正式给予，多为权利或资金。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the native root, the family and idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用本族词根、词族与习语。

normal.en: Old English laenan meant lend; loan came later from Norse.
normal.cn: 古英语 laenan 意为借出；loan 是后来从诺斯语来的。

normal.en: The pair: borrow in, lend out.
normal.cn: 一对：borrow 进，lend 出。

normal.en: Idioms: lend a hand, lend an ear, lend itself to.
normal.cn: 习语：帮一把、倾听、适合于。

normal.en: Past forms: lends, lent, lending, all regular but with short vowel.
normal.cn: 词形：lends、lent、lending，规则但短元音。

normal.en: Banks lend money; sunsets lend warmth.
normal.cn: 银行放贷；落日增添暖意。

abstract.en: Picture a book leaving your shelf with a promise taped on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书带着归还承诺离开书架。

abstract.en: Picture a golden hour pouring warm light over a grey street.
abstract.cn: 想象金色时刻把暖光泼在灰街道上。

abstract.en: Picture two hands passing a ball that must come back.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手传递一个必须回来的球。

examples.en: She lent her notes to everyone before the exam.
examples.cn: 考前她把笔记借给了每个人。

examples.en: Please lend me ten minutes of your time.
examples.cn: 请借我十分钟。

examples.en: The old walls lend the town a quiet dignity.
examples.cn: 老墙给小镇添了安静的庄重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「借的」——借的东西总得还 → 借出

root: 古英语 laenan「借出」，出自日耳曼语 laihiwnjan，与「允许」义词根相关；loan 为诺斯语同族借入。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses keep one gesture: something valuable passes out of your hand for a while — objects, money, qualities, or help.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项保持同一手势：贵重之物暂时离开你的手——物件、钱、品质或帮助。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand offering something that must come back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手，交出终须归还之物。

branches.en: THINGS AND MONEY: the returnable objects leave your hand.
branches.cn: 物与钱：可归还之物离开你的手。

branches.en: ABSTRACT LOAN: warmth, colour and dignity are also lent.
branches.cn: 抽象之借：暖意、色彩与庄重也可出借。

branches.en: HELP ON LOAN: a hand and an ear are offered and taken back.
branches.cn: 出借的帮助：援手与耳朵可借可还。

branches.en: FITTING ITSELF: the thing offers its own qualities to a purpose.
branches.cn: 自我出借：事物把自身特质供给某一用途。

branches.en: THE RETURN TICKET: every lending expects a coming back.
branches.cn: 归还凭据：每次出借都期待归来。

intro.en: Lend is a short native verb with no prefixes; its family adds agent and noun suffixes.
intro.cn: lend 是无前缀的短小本族动词；词族添加施事与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native suffix work.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族后缀加工。

items.example: The verb is native to English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语本族的。
它把 lend 变成 lender。

items.example: The root shows the causative sense.
The idiom keeps the loan idea.
He lent a hand at once.
The hall lends itself to concerts.

definition_zh: 左边的；剩下的（leave 的过去式和过去分词）
definition_en: the side that is opposite the right when facing forward; the past form of leave; remaining
core_image: 面向前方时，心脏偏向的那一侧
scene: 路边停车后他伸手去拉左侧的车门。 Turn left at the second crossing.
sceneCN: 这里 left 是「方向上的左」（第 1 个义项：左边的）；句意为在第二个路口向左转。

pos.zh: leave 的过去式/过去分词：离开；留下

derivatives.zh: left 加 hand 加 -ed，指「惯用左手的」
left 与 over 合成，指「剩余的」

senses.title: The left side or direction
senses.definition: the side opposite the right when a person faces forward
senses.definitionCN: 人面向前方时与右相对的一侧
senses.example: Turn left at the second crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 在第二个路口向左转。
senses.why: Facing forward fixes two sides, and left names the heart-side one.
senses.whyCN: 面向前方定了两侧，left 指心脏所在的一侧。

senses.title: Political left
senses.definition: groups favouring social change and collective welfare
senses.definitionCN: 主张社会变革与集体福利的派别
senses.example: The left pushed for the new labour law.
senses.exampleCN: 左派推动通过了新劳动法。
senses.why: Meeting rooms once placed radicals on the left of the chair, and the seat became the label.
senses.whyCN: 旧时会议厅里激进派坐在议长左侧，座位就成了标签。

senses.title: Remaining
senses.definition: what still exists after the rest is gone or used
senses.definitionCN: 其余部分消失或用完之后还存在的东西
senses.example: There is nothing left in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 锅里什么都不剩了。
senses.why: What leave leaves behind is left: the past participle hardened into a word of its own.
senses.whyCN: leave 留下的东西就是 left：过去分词固化成了独立的词。

senses.title: Past form of leave
senses.definition: the past tense and participle of the verb leave
senses.definitionCN: 动词 leave 的过去式与过去分词
senses.example: He left the office at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他中午离开了办公室。
senses.why: Grammar gives left a second life as a verb form, separate from the direction word.
senses.whyCN: 语法让 left 以动词形式获得第二生命，与方向词分开。

senses.title: A left-hand blow (sport)
senses.definition: in boxing, a punch delivered with the left hand or fist
senses.definitionCN: 拳击中用左手或左拳打出的击打
senses.example: He ended the round with a sharp left.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记凌厉的左拳结束了回合。
senses.why: The side word names the tool used, so the punch borrows the direction.
senses.whyCN: 侧位词命名了使用的工具，于是这一拳借用了方向名。

senses.title: Left-hand side of a page or stage
senses.definition: the left side of an open page, or the stage side from the audience view
senses.definitionCN: 翻开书页的左侧，或观众视角下舞台的左侧
senses.example: The notes sit in the left margin.
senses.exampleCN: 批注在左边的页边。
senses.why: Books and stages keep a fixed geometry, so the side word marks positions on them.
senses.whyCN: 书籍与舞台几何固定，方向词就标出上面的位置。

intro.en: Two words share the spelling left. The direction word comes from Old English left "weak, foolish" (the left hand was the unskilled hand); the verb form is the past of leave.
intro.cn: 两个词共用拼写 left。方向词来自古英语 left「虚弱的、笨拙的」（左手曾是笨拙之手）；动词形式是 leave 的过去式。

items.en: Old English left meant 'weak'; the left hand was thought the clumsy hand, so the side took the name.
items.cn: 古英语 left 意为「虚弱」；左手被视为笨拙之手，这一侧便得了这个名。

items.en: The word is native Germanic; related forms appear as lyft with a sense of 'weak, idle' in northern usage.
items.cn: 该词是日耳曼本族词；北方用法中相关形式 lyft 带「虚弱、闲散」义。

items.en: Middle English fixed left as the standard side word, pushing out older sinistral terms.
items.cn: 中古英语把 left 固定为标准方位词，取代了更老的 sinistral 一类说法。

items.en: Modern English added the political sense from seating customs in assemblies.
items.cn: 现代英语因议会座席习俗新增了政治义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link of the weak-hand word to other Germanic roots is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：「虚弱之手」一词与其他日耳曼词根的联系仍有争议。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects direction and remainder words.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形相近词；第二组收集方向与剩余之词。

entries.definition: To raise or a ride in a car; one letter apart from left, no kinship.
entries.definitionCN: 举起或搭便车；与 left 仅差一字母，无亲缘。

entries.definition: Built from left (past of leave) plus over.
entries.definitionCN: 由 left（leave 的过去式）加 over 构成。

entries.definition: A flat floating platform; only the consonant frame looks close.
entries.definitionCN: 平底漂浮物；只有辅音框架相像。

entries.definition: The other side, also a word for correct.
entries.definitionCN: 另一侧，也表「正确」。

entries.definition: Latin for the left side, later tinted with evil.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语的「左侧」，后染上凶意。

entries.definition: Still present after others are gone; matches the participle sense.
entries.definitionCN: 其余消失后仍在；对应过去分词义。

entries.definition: French for left, meaning socially awkward.
entries.definitionCN: 法语的「左」，转指社交笨拙。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real spellings, seats and phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拼写、座席与短语。

normal.en: Old English left meant 'weak'; the left hand was the clumsy one.
normal.cn: 古英语 left 意为「虚弱」，左手曾是笨拙之手。

normal.en: Turn left, on the left, the left wing are the common phrases.
normal.cn: turn left、on the left、the left wing 是常用短语。

normal.en: Nothing left comes from the past participle of leave.
normal.cn: nothing left 来自 leave 的过去分词。

normal.en: In politics the left and the right came from where members sat.
normal.cn: 政治上的左派右派来自议员的座位。

normal.en: A left in boxing is a left-hand punch.
normal.cn: 拳击里的 left 是左手拳。

abstract.en: Picture your heart leaning to one side when you face north.
abstract.cn: 想象面向北方时心脏偏向一侧。

abstract.en: Picture an empty pot scraped clean, nothing left.
abstract.cn: 想象一口锅被刮得干干净净，什么都不剩。

abstract.en: Picture the assembly hall with reformers seated on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象议会大厅里改革者坐在一侧。

examples.en: The bank is on your left as you come out of the station.
examples.cn: 出车站后银行就在你左手边。

examples.en: Only ten minutes were left before the deadline.
examples.cn: 离截止只剩十分钟。

examples.en: She writes with her left hand.
examples.cn: 她用左手写字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离夫特」——离开后剩下的一侧 → 左边；剩下的

root: 方向词 left 来自古英语 left「虚弱」（左手为笨拙之手）；动词 left 是 leave 的过去式，两者拼写偶合。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses follow two separate histories: a side word that grew political, and a verb form that turned into a word for remainder.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项沿两条独立历史：一个方位词长出政治义，一个动词形式长出「剩余」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the side where the heart sits; and what stays behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：心脏所在的一侧；以及身后剩下的东西。

branches.en: THE SIDE: direction, pages, stages, and the fist that uses it.
branches.cn: 侧位：方向、书页、舞台，以及用到这只手的一拳。

branches.en: THE SEAT: assembly seating turned a side into a movement.
branches.cn: 座席：会议座位把方位变成了派别。

branches.en: WHAT STAYS: the participle hardened into remainder.
branches.cn: 留存之物：过去分词固化成「剩余」。

branches.en: THE VERB FORM: left as the past of leave.
branches.cn: 动词形式：left 作 leave 的过去式。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: facing forward fixes the two sides forever.
branches.cn: 几何：面向前方，两侧永远确定。

intro.en: Left is a short native word with no affixes of its own; compounds and derivatives are formed by attaching English elements.
intro.cn: left 是无词缀的短小本族词；复合词与派生词靠附加英语成分构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is established, so the Latin section stays empty; the items list native compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目列出本族复合词。

items.exampleCN: 一位左撇子击球手上场。

items.example: The leftist wrote for the paper.
items.exampleCN: 那位左派人士为报社撰稿。

items.example: The left wing backed the reform.

items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了更阴暗的色彩。
法语有相同的色彩引申。

definition_zh: 富有的；丰富的；浓郁的
definition_en: having a lot of money or containing a lot of something
core_image: 金色麦田里沉甸甸的麦穗
scene: 这里的土壤肥沃，雨水充足，庄稼长得格外茂盛。 The soil here is rich, the rain is plentiful, and the crops grow especially well.
sceneCN: 这里 rich 是「肥沃的、丰富的」（第 2 个义项：含有大量有益成分）；句意：这里的土壤肥沃，雨水充足，庄稼长得格外茂盛。

senses.title: Wealthy
senses.definition: having a lot of money
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财
senses.example: The rich merchant built a large house.
senses.exampleCN: 这位富商建了一座大房子。
senses.why: The oldest sense is having great wealth.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是拥有大量财富。

senses.title: Full of something
senses.definition: containing a lot of something good
senses.definitionCN: 含有大量有益成分
senses.example: The valley has rich soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷土壤肥沃。
senses.why: Wealth extends from money to any good supply.
senses.whyCN: 财富的含义从金钱延伸到任何充足的资源。

senses.title: Strong in taste
senses.definition: having a strong, full flavor
senses.definitionCN: 味道浓烈饱满
senses.example: The cake is rich in butter and cream.
senses.exampleCN: 这蛋糕黄油和奶油味很浓。
senses.why: A full supply makes food taste full too.
senses.whyCN: 充足的原料让食物味道也饱满。

intro.en: Rich is an old English word from a Germanic root meaning powerful.
intro.cn: rich 是古英语词，来自意为「有权势」的日耳曼词根。

items.en: Rice means powerful or wealthy.
items.cn: rice 意为有权势的或富有的。

items.en: The root is linked to rulers.
items.cn: 这个词根与统治者有关。

items.en: Rex, king, is a distant relative.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rex（国王）是远亲。

items.en: Rich first means powerful and then wealthy.
items.cn: rich 先指有权势，再指富有。

items.en: It also means full of something.
items.cn: 它也指充满某物。

note.en: Rich is about having much; wealthy stresses money and property.
note.cn: rich 强调拥有得多；wealthy 更强调钱财与财产。

entries.definition: wealth
entries.definitionCN: 财富

entries.definition: in a full or generous way
entries.definitionCN: 丰富地

entries.definition: the quality of being rich
entries.definitionCN: 丰富

entries.definition: having a lot of money
entries.definitionCN: 富有的

entries.definition: existing in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 充足的

entries.definition: able to produce good crops
entries.definitionCN: 肥沃的

normalIntro.en: Rich is a field heavy with grain and a pocket full of coins.
normalIntro.cn: rich 是沉甸甸的麦田与装满硬币的口袋。

normal.en: Rich soil grows strong crops.
normal.cn: 肥沃的土壤长出茁壮的庄稼。

normal.en: The rich often give to charities.
normal.cn: 富人常常捐助慈善。

normal.en: Rich flavor means a strong taste.
normal.cn: rich flavor 意为浓郁的味道。

normal.en: A country rich in oil has much oil.
normal.cn: a country rich in oil 是石油丰富的国家。

normal.en: Compare wealthy: wealthy stresses money, rich can mean full of anything.
normal.cn: 对比 wealthy：wealthy 强调钱财，rich 可指充满任何东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wheat field bending under its own weight.
abstract.cn: 想象麦田因麦穗沉重而弯下。

abstract.en: Imagine a cup filled to the very edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一只倒到杯口的杯子。

abstract.en: Think of a voice that fills a whole hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个充满整个大厅的声音。

examples.en: He grew rich through hard work.
examples.cn: 他靠努力工作富了起来。

examples.en: The region is rich in minerals.
examples.cn: 这个地区矿产丰富。

examples.en: This soup has a rich flavor.
examples.cn: 这汤味道浓郁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rich」四个字母——r 像饱满的麦穗，ich 读来厚实，像装满的口袋。

root: 古英语 rice（有权势的、富有的）→ rich，核心义「拥有很多、内容充足」。

sensesIntro.en: Rich starts with wealth, extends to any abundant supply, and then to full flavor.
sensesIntro.cn: rich 从财富开始，延伸到任何充足的供给，再指浓郁的味道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a golden wheat field heavy with grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：麦穗沉甸甸的金色麦田。

branches.en: Wealth is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 财富是最古老的含义。

branches.en: Any good supply counts as richness.
branches.cn: 任何充足的资源都算丰富。

branches.en: Food with full ingredients tastes rich.
branches.cn: 原料充足的食物味道浓郁。

branches.en: Money and soil are both forms of plenty.
branches.cn: 金钱与土壤都是丰足的形式。

branches.en: A full supply makes a full taste.
branches.cn: 充足的供给带来饱满的味道。

intro.en: Rich is an old English adjective from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: rich 是来自日耳曼词根的古英语形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rex, king, is a distant cousin of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rex（国王）是这个词根的远亲。

items.example: Rice is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: rice 是现存最古老的形式。
rikja 把财富与权力联系起来。

latinEntries.example: Rex is related to the Germanic root.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rex 与这个日耳曼词根有亲缘关系。

definition_zh: 解释；说明；讲解；阐明原因
definition_en: to make something clear or easy to understand by giving details or reasons
core_image: 把一团乱麻摊开在桌上：一根一根理顺，直到谁都能看清纹路
scene: 弟弟看不懂棋盘上为什么输，哥哥把每一步摆回原位，指着棋子说： Let me explain why your knight lost the game.
sceneCN: 这里 explain 指「把道理讲清楚」（第 1 个义项：说明使易于理解）；句意为哥哥解释输棋的原因。

collocations.zh: 为自己的言行说明理由

derivatives.zh: 解释；说明（explain 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「摊开说明的过程或结果」）
解释性的；说明的（explanation 加形容词后缀，义为「用于说明的」）
可解释的；可理解的（同根形容词，义为「能被摊开的」）
无法解释的（in- 加 explicable，义为「摊不开、说不清的」）

senses.title: To make something easy to understand
senses.definition: to give details or reasons so that something becomes clear
senses.definitionCN: 通过给出细节或原因，使某事变得清楚易懂
senses.example: Let me explain why your knight lost the game.
senses.exampleCN: 让我来解释为什么你的马输了这局棋。
senses.why: The Latin root is to flatten out: a tangled thing is spread open level, so its folds show plainly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是「摊平」：把一团乱的东西摊平展开，褶皱就看得清清楚楚。

senses.title: To give reasons for one's behaviour
senses.titleCN: 为自己的言行说明理由
senses.definition: to tell why you did or said something
senses.definitionCN: 说出你为何这么做、这么说
senses.example: He was asked to explain his absence at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他被要求说明为什么没来开会。
senses.why: The spreading act turns inward: now your own conduct is the tangle laid flat.
senses.whyCN: 摊开的动作转向自身：这次被摊平的是你自己的行为。

senses.title: To be the reason behind something
senses.definition: to be the cause that makes something happen or make sense
senses.definitionCN: 作为让某事发生或说得通的缘由
senses.example: Her long silence explains the sudden change.
senses.exampleCN: 她的长期沉默解释了这场突然的转变。
senses.why: Once the knot is spread open, its shape alone shows why the thread ran as it did.
senses.whyCN: 乱麻摊开后，它的形状本身就说明了线为何这样走。

senses.title: To give reasons for something unfortunate
senses.definition: to make clear why something bad happened, often to excuse it
senses.definitionCN: 说明坏事为何发生，常带开脱意味
senses.example: Nothing can explain the loss except pure bad luck.
senses.exampleCN: 除了运气太差，这场失利没有别的缘由。
senses.why: The same opening-up applied to failure: laying the accident flat to see what bent it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的展开用在失败上：把事故摊平，看清是哪里折了。

intro.en: Explain comes from Latin explanare, "to make level, to flatten out", a root image of spreading things flat.
intro.cn: explain 源自拉丁语 explanare「弄平、摊开」，词根画面是把东西摊平展开。

items.en: Latin explanare meant "to flatten, to make level", from ex- (out) + planus (flat, level).
items.cn: 拉丁语 explanare 意为「弄平、摊平」，由 ex-（向外）+ planus（平的）构成。

items.en: The plain in explain is the same word family as plane and plan: something spread out evenly.
items.cn: explain 里的 plain 与 plane、plan 同族：都是被均匀摊开的东西。

items.en: Confusion with the similar plain gave the spelling its extra i in English.
items.cn: 与 plain 的混淆让英语拼写里多了一个 i。

items.en: Middle English took explain and explanen from Latin in the fifteenth century, meaning to make clear.
items.cn: 十五世纪中古英语从拉丁语借入，义为「讲清楚」。

items.en: Modern English settled the spelling explain and kept the flat-image in phrases like explain away.
items.cn: 现代英语定形为 explain，摊平意象保留在 explain away 等短语中。

note.en: These neighbours share the planus root or the act of making things clear.
note.cn: 下列词与 explain 同根，或同样有「讲清楚」的动作。

entries.definition: the act or result of explaining
entries.definitionCN: 解释；说明（同根名词）

entries.definition: level, clear, simple
entries.definitionCN: 平的；清楚的；朴素的（同词根形容词）

entries.definition: a drawing spread out on a surface
entries.definitionCN: 平面图；计划（同词根，被摊开的东西）

entries.definition: to unfold in detail
entries.definitionCN: 详细说明（同根异形，来自 plicare「折叠」一族）

entries.definition: to make clearer
entries.definitionCN: 澄清（偏把混浊变清）

entries.definition: to explain the meaning of
entries.definitionCN: 诠释；口译（偏意义转换）

entries.definition: to explain the cause of
entries.definitionCN: 说明原因（偏交代缘由）

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root and usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根与用法的联想。

normal.en: ex- (out) + plain (flat): spread the tangle flat to see it.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ plain（平）：把乱团摊平才看得清。

normal.en: Plain is the family word: a plain statement needs no more explaining.
normal.cn: plain 是同族词：平实的陈述无需再多解释。

normal.en: Explanation is the noun: write your explanation on paper.
normal.cn: explanation 是名词：把解释写在纸上。

normal.en: Explain away means to flatten a fault until it looks small.
normal.cn: explain away 是把错误摊平到看起来很小。

normal.en: Explicable things can be spread open; inexplicable ones cannot.
normal.cn: explicable 能被摊开，inexplicable 摊不开。

abstract.en: Picture a knotted rope laid out on a table, straightened thread by thread.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一根打了结的绳，被一寸寸理直。

abstract.en: A good explanation is a map: folded land becomes flat paper.
abstract.cn: 好的解释是一张地图：起伏的大地摊平成纸。

abstract.en: When you explain yourself, the knot on the table is your own behaviour.
abstract.cn: 当你 explain yourself，桌上那团乱麻就是你的行为。

examples.en: Let me explain why your knight lost the game.
examples.cn: 让我来解释为什么你的马输了这局棋。

examples.en: He was asked to explain his absence at the meeting.
examples.cn: 他被要求说明为什么没来开会。

examples.en: Her long silence explains the sudden change.
examples.cn: 她的长期沉默解释了这场突然的转变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗死普雷恩」——死磕到一块平地上，把道理讲得平平整整。

root: 源自拉丁语 explanare「弄平、摊开」，由 ex-（向外）+ planus（平的）构成；plain、plane、plan 同族。英语因与 plain 混淆而定形为 explain。中古英语十五世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: From flattening a knot into view, the word covers teaching, self-justification, and causes laid bare.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把结摊平给人看」出发，覆盖讲解、自我辩解与摆明缘由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tangle spread out flat on a table
core.cn: 核心意象：乱麻被摊平在桌上

branches.en: the tangle opened so a learner can see
branches.cn: 乱团被摊开给学习者看

branches.en: one's own conduct as the opened knot
branches.cn: 被摊开的是自己的行为

branches.en: the opened shape itself shows the cause
branches.cn: 摊开的形状本身显出缘由

branches.en: failure laid flat to find the bend
branches.cn: 把失败摊平找折点

branches.en: making clear and giving reasons are one act
branches.cn: 讲清楚与给原因是一体

intro.en: The family rests on planus (flat) with the outward prefix ex-.
intro.cn: 词族立足于 planus（平），加向外前缀 ex-。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins from the planus root.
latinIntro.cn: planus 词根的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 工业；行业；勤劳
definition_en: the business of making goods in factories, a branch of trade, or hard steady work
core_image: 轰鸣的流水线：原料进去，产品出来
scene: 河边的新厂区里机器连成一片。 The car industry employs thousands of workers.
sceneCN: 这里 industry 是「行业」（第 2 个义项：某类产业）；句意：汽车行业雇用数千名工人。

derivatives.zh: industry 加形容词后缀，义为「工业的」
industrial 加动词后缀，义为「工业化」
同根形容词，义为「勤奋的」

senses.title: Manufacturing as a whole
senses.definition: the production of goods in factories
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里生产商品的活动
senses.example: The region depends on heavy industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区依靠重工业。
senses.why: A whole plain of chimneys makes the goods.
senses.whyCN: 一整片烟囱造出商品。

senses.title: A branch of trade
senses.definition: one particular line of business
senses.definitionCN: 某一类经营活动
senses.example: The tourist industry grew fast.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业发展很快。
senses.why: One belt of the great machine is named after its goods.
senses.whyCN: 大机器的一条带子以它的商品命名。

senses.title: Hard steady work
senses.definition: working hard and steadily
senses.definitionCN: 努力而持续地工作
senses.example: Her industry impressed the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她的勤奋给老师留下深刻印象。
senses.why: The factory never stops, and neither does the worker.
senses.whyCN: 工厂不停，工人也不停。

senses.title: Industrial companies collectively
senses.definition: the companies and people who run factories
senses.definitionCN: 经营工厂的公司与人群
senses.example: Industry has asked for lower taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 工业界要求减税。
senses.why: All chimneys speak with one voice.
senses.whyCN: 所有烟囱用一个声音说话。

intro.en: Industry comes from Latin industria, meaning diligence, built on indu- (within) and the root ofstruere (to build up). The meaning shifted from hard work to organized production.
intro.cn: industry 来自拉丁语 industria「勤奋」，由 indu-「在内」与词根 struere「建造」构成；词义从辛勤劳作转移到有组织的生产。

items.en: Latin struere meant to build, pile up; it gave structure and construct.
items.cn: 拉丁语 struere 意为建造、堆积；同根词有 structure 与 construct。

items.en: industria meant diligence, a constant building-up of effort.
items.cn: 拉丁语 industria 意为勤勉，即持续积累的努力。

items.en: Old French industrie carried the sense of ability and activity.
items.cn: 古法语 industrie 带有才能与活动之意。

items.en: Middle English industrie first meant cleverness and diligence.
items.cn: 中古英语 industrie 最初指机敏与勤勉。

items.en: The industrial revolution gave it the factory sense we use most today.
items.cn: 工业革命赋予它今天最常用的工厂含义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the build-root family. The meaning group compares words of trade and work.
note.cn: 形近组收录「建造」词根词族；词义组比较表示行业与劳作的词。

entries.definition: the adjective of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 同族形容词。

entries.definition: hard-working, the older sense kept.
entries.definitionCN: 勤奋的，保留了旧义。

entries.definition: plural of industry.
entries.definitionCN: industry 的复数。

entries.definition: trade in general or one firm.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生意或一家公司。

entries.definition: the activity of buying and selling.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖活动。

entries.definition: careful steady effort.
entries.definitionCN: 认真持续的努力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the build root, the factory sense and the industrious twin.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「建造」词根、工厂义与 industrious 孪生词。

normal.en: in- plus struere (build): effort built up inside a person.
normal.cn: in- 加 struere（建造）：人内心垒起的努力。

normal.en: structure and construct share the same build root.
normal.cn: structure 与 construct 共享同一建造词根。

normal.en: the tourist industry: one belt of the machine.
normal.cn: the tourist industry：大机器的一条带子。

normal.en: industrious kept the old meaning of hard work.
normal.cn: industrious 保留了辛勤工作的旧义。

normal.en: the industrial revolution renamed the word.
normal.cn: 工业革命重新命名了这个词。

abstract.en: One image: a chimney plain breathing smoke in rows.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：烟囱成排，呼出白烟。

abstract.en: Industry is effort piled up until it becomes a trade.
abstract.cn: industry 是垒起来的努力，垒到成了行业。

abstract.en: The worker and the factory share one heartbeat.
abstract.cn: 工人与工厂共享同一个心跳。

examples.en: Steel industry moved the whole town forward.
examples.cn: 钢铁工业带动了整个小镇。

examples.en: The fashion industry sets trends each season.
examples.cn: 时尚业每季引领潮流。

examples.en: Success needs talent and industry together.
examples.cn: 成功需要天赋与勤奋兼备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因达斯特里」：在达城里辛勤开工厂， industry。

root: 拉丁语 indu-「在内」+ struere「建造」→ industria「勤勉」→ 古法语 industrie「才能、活动」→ 中古英语 industrie「勤勉」→ 现代英语增加「工业、行业」义；同根词 structure、construct、instrument。

sensesIntro.en: Industry is the endless machine: the whole of manufacturing, one named trade, the diligence behind it, and the voice of all factories.
sensesIntro.cn: industry 是不歇的机器：制造业整体、被命名的某一行业、背后的勤奋，以及所有工厂的合唱。

core.en: Effort built up like a wall until it becomes a whole machine of production.
core.cn: 努力像砌墙般层层垒起，直到成为整套生产机器。

branches.en: MANUFACTURE: the region depends on heavy industry.
branches.cn: 制造：该地区依靠重工业。

branches.en: TRADE: the tourist industry grew fast.
branches.cn: 行业：旅游业发展迅速。

branches.en: DILIGENCE: her industry impressed the teacher.
branches.cn: 勤勉：她的勤奋令人印象深刻。

branches.en: VOICE: industry has asked for lower taxes.
branches.cn: 声音：工业界要求减税。

branches.en: SCALE: production measured in whole trades.
branches.cn: 规模：以整条行业计量的生产。

intro.en: Industry builds industrial, industrialize and industrious.
intro.cn: industry 构成 industrial、industrialize 与 industrious。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the building verb struere behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的建造动词 struere。

items.example: An industrial zone lies east of the city.
The bridge has a steel structure.

definition_zh: 葡萄酒；酒；果酒；（引申）令人陶醉之物
definition_en: an alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes or other fruit, and by extension anything that intoxicates
core_image: 烛光里一只高脚杯轻轻一晃，深红的液体贴上杯壁又缓缓流回去
scene: 节日的餐桌上，主人给每只高脚杯倒上深红的酒，烛光在杯壁上一晃一晃。 A bottle of red wine was opened to celebrate the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 wine 是「葡萄酒」（第 1 个义项：用葡萄发酵制成的酒）；句意为开了一瓶红葡萄酒来庆祝丰收。烛光里那只杯壁上深红的液体，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The drink of crushed grapes
senses.definition: an alcoholic drink made by letting grape juice ferment, kept in bottles and served with meals
senses.definitionCN: 让葡萄汁发酵而成的酒，装在瓶里，佐餐饮用
senses.example: A bottle of red wine was opened to celebrate the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 开了一瓶红葡萄酒来庆祝丰收。
senses.why: The word first named the vine itself and its juice, and the drink kept the name as the products spread.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指葡萄藤及其汁液，随着这些产物传播，饮品保留了名字。

senses.title: Fruit drinks of the same kind
senses.definition: a similar fermented drink made from other fruits, such as plum, apple or pear
senses.definitionCN: 用李子、苹果、梨等其他水果发酵而成的同类饮品
senses.example: Grandmother made pear wine in a big jar every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母每年秋天都用大罐子酿梨酒。
senses.why: Once wine meant fermented fruit juice, any fruit could fill the bottle without changing the word.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 wine 表示发酵果汁，任何水果都能装进这只瓶子而不改词。

senses.title: Something that intoxicates
senses.definition: in literature, anything that lifts the mind like drink, such as joy, praise or freedom
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中，指像酒一样让人心飘起来的东西，如喜悦、赞美或自由
senses.example: The wine of first love made him deaf to all advice.
senses.exampleCN: 初恋这杯酒让他听不进任何劝告。
senses.why: The physical warmth of drink became a picture for any strong feeling that carries reason away.
senses.whyCN: 酒带来的那点身体的暖，成了任何强得足以带走理智的情感的样子。

intro.en: Wine is one of Europe's oldest loanwords: Latin vinum stood behind Old English win well before England had vineyards.
intro.cn: wine 是欧洲最古老的借词之一：早在英格兰有葡萄园之前，拉丁语 vinum 就已经站在古英语 win 的背后。

items.en: vinum meant wine, and the word travelled with Roman traders and soldiers.
items.cn: vinum 意为葡萄酒，这个词随罗马商人与士兵一路传播。

items.en: The Germanic tribes borrowed it early, giving forms such as wīn before any written record.
items.cn: 日耳曼部落很早就借入了它，在有文字记录之前就出现了 wīn 这样的形式。

items.en: win named the drink as well as the vine, and appears in laws on trade and feasts.
items.cn: win 既指饮品也指葡萄藤，出现在关于贸易与宴会的法令里。

items.en: Wine settled into the spelling with a silent e, and became the common word at table.
items.cn: 中古英语时拼写加上不发音的 e，成为餐桌上常用的词。

items.en: The word widened to other fruit drinks and lent its warmth to poetry about joy and love.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到其他果酒，并把它的暖意借给了关于喜悦与爱的诗。

note.en: The first group collects spirits and drinks that look or sound similar, the second beverages and the vine.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的酒与饮品，第二组收饮料与葡萄藤相关的词。

entries.definition: The plant that bears grapes.
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄藤

entries.definition: Air moving across the land.
entries.definitionCN: 风

entries.definition: To come out on top.
entries.definitionCN: 赢

entries.definition: A long high complaining sound.
entries.definitionCN: 抱怨的尖声

entries.definition: An alcoholic drink made from grain.
entries.definitionCN: 啤酒

entries.definition: Strong distilled drink.
entries.definitionCN: 烈酒

entries.definition: The fruit from which wine is pressed.
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄

normalIntro.en: Wine is short but often confused with vine; the missing first letter is the whole story of a drink made from a vine.
normalIntro.cn: wine 很短，却常与 vine 混；少掉的那个首字母，正是「藤上长出来的酒」的故事。

normal.en: Vine is the plant, and wine is what the plant becomes once pressed.
normal.cn: vine 是藤，wine 是藤被压榨之后变成的东西。

normal.en: The silent e stays quiet, as in fine and line.
normal.cn: 末尾的 e 不发音，和 fine、line 一样。

normal.en: Wine begins with w for the round top of a glass in profile.
normal.cn: wine 以 w 开头，像侧看的杯口那道弧线。

normal.en: One glass of red, two of white: both keep the same short word.
normal.cn: 一杯红的，两杯白的，用的都是这同一个短词。

normal.en: Wine and dine is a rhyme pair you can hear across a dinner table.
normal.cn: wine and dine 是一对押韵的说法，在餐桌那头都听得见。

abstract.en: Deep red liquid clinging to the inside of a glass.
abstract.cn: 深红的液体贴在杯壁内侧。

abstract.en: The small pop of a cork and a burst of dark scent.
abstract.cn: 软木塞一声轻响，涌出一阵深色的香气。

abstract.en: A voice warming up two chairs further along.
abstract.cn: 隔了两个座位，有个人的声音变暖了。

examples.en: They drank a little wine with the fish.
examples.cn: 他们吃鱼时喝了一点葡萄酒。

examples.en: This wine is made from apples rather than grapes.
examples.cn: 这种酒是用苹果而不是葡萄做的。

examples.en: The village has been making wine for four hundred years.
examples.cn: 这个村子酿酒已有四百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: vine（藤）少一个字母、换个首音就成了 wine —— 藤上结的果子酿成「葡萄酒」。

root: 拉丁语 vinum（葡萄酒）→ 日耳曼语借入 wīn → 古英语 win → 中古英语 wine；同族有 vine、winery、winegrower。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the fermented juice of grapes, widens to other fruits, and finally becomes a picture for anything that makes the heart light.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从发酵的葡萄汁开始，扩展到其他水果，最后成为一切让心变轻之物的图画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red liquid turning slowly against a candlelit glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：烛光里深红液体在杯中慢慢打转。

branches.en: The table branch: a bottle opened for the harvest.
branches.cn: 餐桌分支：为丰收开瓶。

branches.en: The orchard branch: pear wine in a big jar.
branches.cn: 果园分支：大罐子里的梨酒。

branches.en: The poetic branch: first love as a drink.
branches.cn: 诗意分支：初恋如一杯酒。

branches.en: The material branch: whatever fruit is available fills the bottle.
branches.cn: 材料分支：有什么果子就装什么瓶子。

branches.en: The extension branch: taste first, then the mind.
branches.cn: 延伸分支：先是舌头，后是心。

intro.en: Wine is a borrowed stem that builds few but useful compounds: winery, wineglass and the verb wine and dine.
intro.cn: wine 是借入的词干，构成的复合词不多但很实用：winery、wineglass，以及 wine and dine 这一说法。

latinIntro.en: The whole word family goes back to Latin vinum, so the Latin column here is the true source, not a cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都回到拉丁语 vinum，所以这里的拉丁栏是真正的来源，而不是远亲。
