definition_zh: 邀请；招待；招致（麻烦、批评）
definition_en: to ask someone to come somewhere or do something, or to make something likely to happen
core_image: 一扇门被推开，主人朝外伸出手做个「请进」的姿势
scene: 周末的厨房里炖着汤，主人擦擦手，走到门口朝对面的邻居招手。 She invited the whole street to dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 invite 是「邀请」（第 1 个义项：请别人来），句意为她请了整条街的人来吃晚饭。画面里的物件：汤锅、门口、手巾。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「邀请；邀请函」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「诱人的」
由本词加 -ee 构成，义为「被邀请者」
由本词加 -ional 构成，义为「邀请制的」

senses.title: Asking someone to come
senses.definition: to ask a person politely to come to an event or a place
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请人到某个活动或某个地方来
senses.example: They invited us to the wedding in June.
senses.exampleCN: 他们邀请我们参加六月的婚礼。
senses.why: Latin invitare meant "to ask, to entertain", with no need for a written card.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invitare 意为「邀请、款待」，那时还不需要请柬。

senses.title: Offering hospitality
senses.definition: to receive someone as a guest and provide food or lodging
senses.definitionCN: 把某人当客人接来，并提供饭食或住处
senses.example: A neighbour invited the stranded family in for tea.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居把滞留的那家人请进屋喝茶。
senses.why: The same verb covers the welcome itself, not just the asking.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也涵盖「招待」这件事，而不只是开口请。

senses.title: Bringing trouble on yourself
senses.definition: to make something bad or unwanted more likely by your own action
senses.definitionCN: 因为自己的举动让不好的事情更容易发生
senses.example: Leaving the gate open invites trouble at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里不关院门是会招来麻烦的。
senses.why: The "trouble" sense is the welcoming gesture aimed at something harmful.
senses.whyCN: 「招麻烦」义就是同一个欢迎手势，只是指向了有害的东西。

senses.title: Welcoming a response
senses.definition: to openly welcome comments, questions, or applications
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示乐于接受意见、提问或报名
senses.example: The paper invites readers to send in photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸欢迎读者寄来照片。
senses.why: A request for replies is still an invitation, only written to many at once.
senses.whyCN: 征集回应仍是邀请，只不过一次写给许多人。

intro.en: Invite has kept its original meaning of asking and welcoming almost unchanged for two thousand years.
intro.cn: invite 两千年来几乎原封不动地保留了「邀请、款待」的原意。

items.en: invitare meant "to ask, to treat as a guest".
items.cn: invitare 意为「邀请、当客人款待」。

items.en: The noun invitatus recorded the welcoming of a guest.
items.cn: 名词 invitatus 记载了对客人的接待。

items.en: French had inviter, used for asking someone over.
items.cn: 法语有 inviter，用于请人过来。

items.en: English shortened the French verb to invite.
items.cn: 英语把法语动词缩成 invite。

items.en: The sense of inviting trouble grew from the idea of welcoming.
items.cn: 「招来麻烦」义从「迎接」的想法里长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invi- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for asking people in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invi- 开头；近义组收表示请人进来的词。

entries.definition: A spoken or written request to come.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「邀请；请柬」，同族词。

entries.definition: To put money or effort in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」，开头相同。

entries.definition: To make something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」，只差一个字母。

entries.definition: The general verb for requesting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「请；问」，最泛。

entries.definition: To greet someone with pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「欢迎」，强调态度。

entries.definition: To order someone to come.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「传唤」，带命令色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks put the word at a door being held open.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它放在一扇被扶开的门口。

normal.en: The old verb invitare meant to ask and to treat well.
normal.cn: 古动词 invitare 既指邀请，也指好好招待。

normal.en: What arrives in the post is an invitation.
normal.cn: 寄到手里的东西叫 invitation。

normal.en: The person who receives it is the invitee.
normal.cn: 收到邀请的人叫 invitee。

normal.en: Leave a door open and you invite the wind.
normal.cn: 门留着不关，就是把风请进来。

normal.en: Invite a question and you are glad to hear it.
normal.cn: invite questions 就是欢迎别人提问。

abstract.en: Invitation is a door left open on purpose.
abstract.cn: 邀请就是一扇有意留开的门。

abstract.en: Whatever you welcome decides what follows you home.
abstract.cn: 你欢迎什么，什么就跟你回家。

abstract.en: Inviting trouble is the same gesture, aimed badly.
abstract.cn: 招麻烦是同一个手势，只是指错了方向。

examples.en: She invited two former students back to speak at the school.
examples.cn: 她请了两位往届学生回校演讲。

examples.en: The narrow path invites people to walk faster than they should.
examples.cn: 这条窄路会引诱人走得比该有的速度快。

examples.en: The magazine invites letters from readers of any age.
examples.cn: 这本杂志欢迎任何年龄的读者来信。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进来）+ vite（拉丁 invitare 邀请）——请你进来

root: 拉丁语 invitare「邀请；款待」→ 古法语 inviter → 英语 invite。同族有 invitation、invitee、inviting。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: asking someone over, receiving a guest, drawing trouble, and welcoming replies.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：请人来、招待客人、招来麻烦，以及欢迎回应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out as the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：门开时伸出的那只手。

branches.en: THE CARD: a written or spoken request to come.
branches.cn: 请柬这条线：写出来或说出口的请。

branches.en: THE TABLE: food and shelter given to a guest.
branches.cn: 饭桌这条线：给客人的饭食与住处。

branches.en: THE GATE: an open entry that lets trouble in.
branches.cn: 院门这条线：留开的通道把麻烦放进来。

branches.en: THE OPENNESS: both senses come from a willing yes.
branches.cn: 敞开这条线：两个义项都源于一个乐意的「好」。

branches.en: THE RESULT: what you welcome decides what arrives.
branches.cn: 结果这条线：你欢迎什么，就决定什么到来。

intro.en: Invite keeps a single Latin stem, invit-, plus the verb ending -e.
intro.cn: invite 由一个拉丁词干 invit- 加动词尾 -e 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin invitare and invitatus are both recorded with the friendly sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 invitare 与 invitatus 均有记载，都带友好的意味。

items.example: The root survives in invite and invitation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根仍见于 invite 与 invitation。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
The participle shows the noun form.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词显示名词形式。

definition_zh: 关系；亲属；交往
definition_en: a connection between two or more things; a member of one's family; the way people or countries deal with each other
core_image: 家谱图上两条分支在同一个名字处交汇
scene: 摊开的家谱图上，两条支线在同一个名字处交汇。 There is no relation between the two numbers.
sceneCN: 这里 relation 是「关联」（第 1 个义项：事物之间的联系）；句意为这两个数字之间没有关联。画面里可留意：家谱图上交汇的两条支线。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two or more things are connected or affect each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个事物相互连接或影响的方式
senses.example: There is no relation between the two numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个数字之间没有关联。
senses.why: The noun names what is produced when one thing is carried back to another: a line drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名「把一物带回另一物」时产生的东西：两者之间画出的一条线。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: She is a distant relation of the old painter.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那位老画家的远亲。
senses.why: Kinship is the oldest form of connection, so the word for a link also names the people joined by it.
senses.whyCN: 血缘是最古老的连接形式，因此表「联系」的词也用来指被这条线连起来的人。

senses.title: Official dealings
senses.definition: the way groups or countries deal with one another, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 团体或国家之间往来的方式，通常用复数
senses.example: The two countries restored diplomatic relations after ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在十年之后恢复了外交关系。
senses.why: States also stand in relation to each other, and the plural names the whole web of those dealings.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间也彼此处于关系之中，复数形式便命名这整张往来之网。

intro.en: Relation is the noun of relate, and like refer it comes from the Latin verb of carrying back.
intro.cn: relation 是 relate 的名词，与 refer 一样出自拉丁语表「带回」的动词。

items.en: Referre meant to carry back and to report, built on ferre, to carry.
items.cn: referre 意为带回与报告，由 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Relatio named a bringing back, and Latin writers used it for a report to a body and for a logical connection.
items.cn: relatio 指一种带回，拉丁作家用它表示向机构作报告，也表示逻辑上的关联。

items.en: Old French relacion carried the sense of a report and of a connection between things.
items.cn: 古法语 relacion 兼具「报告」与「事物之间关联」两义。

items.en: English extended the noun to people connected by blood, since kinship is a relation in the plainest sense.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词扩展到有血缘的人，因为亲属是最直白的一种关系。

items.en: In the plural, relations came to name the official dealings between states and groups.
items.cn: 在复数形式中，relations 用来指国家与团体之间的正式往来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns of the same carrying family; the near-meaning group gathers words for connection and kinship.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词族的名词；近义组收表示联系与亲属的词。

entries.definition: A continuing connection between people.
entries.definitionCN: 关系；关联。

entries.definition: A member of one's family.
entries.definitionCN: 亲戚。

entries.definition: A mention or a source.
entries.definitionCN: 提及；参考。

entries.definition: A link between things.
entries.definitionCN: 联系；连接。

entries.definition: Something that joins two things.
entries.definitionCN: 联系；环节。

entries.definition: Family relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 亲属关系。

entries.definition: A mental or official connection.
entries.definitionCN: 联想；协会。

normalIntro.en: The noun names the line drawn between two things, the people joined by blood, and the dealings between states.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词指两物之间画出的那条线、被血缘连起来的人，以及国家之间的往来。

normal.en: Relate is the act, relation is the line it draws.
normal.cn: relate 是动作，relation 是它画出的线。

normal.en: In relation to means with regard to.
normal.cn: in relation to 意为关于、相对于。

normal.en: A close relation is a near relative, not a near idea.
normal.cn: a close relation 指近亲，不是相近的想法。

normal.en: Diplomatic relations are kept in the plural.
normal.cn: diplomatic relations 用复数。

normal.en: Public relations is the work of managing how people see you.
normal.cn: public relations 是管理公众看法的行当。

abstract.en: A relation is not a thing but a line between things.
abstract.cn: 关系不是一个东西，而是东西之间的一条线。

abstract.en: Every relation changes both sides a little.
abstract.cn: 每一种关系都会稍稍改变双方。

abstract.en: To bear no relation to something is to share no line with it.
abstract.cn: 与某物毫无关系，就是与它不共用任何一条线。

examples.en: There is no relation between the two numbers.
examples.cn: 这两个数字之间没有关联。

examples.en: She is a distant relation of the old painter.
examples.cn: 她是那位老画家的远亲。

examples.en: The two countries restored diplomatic relations after ten years.
examples.cn: 两国在十年之后恢复了外交关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: relate（联系）加 ion（名词尾）：被联系起来的这条线是关联，被这条线连起来的人是亲属，国与国之间的线是交往。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回、报告）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 拉丁 relatio（带回、关联）→ 古法语 relacion → 英语 relation；同族有 relate、relationship、relative、relational。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line drawn by carrying one thing back to another; the senses move from a link between things, to people joined by blood, to dealings between states.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把一物带回另一物所画出的线」；义项从事物之间的联系，到被血缘连起来的人，再到国家之间的往来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two branches of a family tree meeting at one name.
core.cn: 核心意象：家谱图上两条分支在同一个名字处交汇。

branches.en: two figures with no line between
branches.cn: 之间没有线的两个数字

branches.en: a distant cousin at a funeral
branches.cn: 葬礼上的一位远亲

branches.en: two embassies reopened
branches.cn: 重新开馆的两国使馆

branches.en: a line between numbers and a line between people
branches.cn: 数字之间的线与人与人之间的线

branches.en: family ties and state ties
branches.cn: 家族纽带与国家纽带

intro.en: The noun of carrying back takes the Latin ending of action, and the result names both a logical link and a family tie.
intro.cn: 表「带回」的名词接上拉丁表行为的词尾，结果便同时命名逻辑上的关联与家族中的纽带。

latinIntro.en: The base is relatus, carried back, with -io forming the noun relatio.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 relatus（被带回的），-io 构成名词 relatio。

definition_zh: 可能的；能做到的；很可能的；合适的；尽可能好的
definition_en: able to be done or to happen; likely but not certain; suitable in the circumstances
core_image: 一扇没有上锁的门：门后有路，但还没有人迈出去
scene: 面试结束后，年轻人站在公司门口，反复回想自己还有没有机会。 The recruiter said a second interview was possible if the first one went well.
sceneCN: 这里是「有可能的」（第 1 个义项：事情能够发生）；句意为招聘人员说，如果初面顺利，二面是有可能的。画面里可留意的是那扇半开的门和候选人握着的手。

pos.zh: 可能的；能做到的；很可能的；合适的

derivatives.zh: possible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，指「可能性」，-ity 把形容词变成抽象名词
possible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，表示「也许；可能地」
否定前缀 im- 加 possible 构成，表示「不可能的」

senses.title: Able to be done or achieved
senses.definition: able to happen or be done, because nothing stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 因为不存在阻碍，所以能够发生或做到
senses.example: A cure for the disease may be possible within ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年之内或许有可能找到这种病的疗法。
senses.why: The Latin verb posse means to be able; the first sense is bare ability with no obstacle in front of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 posse 意为「能够」，所以这个词最初的义项就是「有能力、又没阻碍」。

senses.title: Likely to be true or to happen
senses.definition: having a strong chance of being true or of happening, though not certain
senses.definitionCN: 成真或发生的几率很大，但并不确定
senses.example: It is possible that the train will be late again.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟火车很可能再次晚点。
senses.why: Once a thing can happen, the same word is used for what a speaker judges will probably happen, so ability shades into likelihood.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然能够发生，说话人就用同一个词来表达自己判断「大概会发生」，于是「能力」之外又添了「几率」。

senses.title: Suitable in a particular situation
senses.definition: acceptable or suitable for a purpose or a person, given the limits of the situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情境的限制下，对某个目的或某个人来说是合适、可接受的
senses.example: She is the only possible candidate for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这份工作唯一合适的人选。
senses.why: If something can be done, it can also be chosen; the word then judges fitness instead of bare ability.
senses.whyCN: 一件事只要做得到，就可以被选中，于是这个词从「能不能」转为评判「合不合适」。

senses.title: As good as the situation allows
senses.definition: used after a superlative or with all, meaning the best that the circumstances permit
senses.definitionCN: 用于最高级之后或与 all 连用，表示在现有条件下能达到的最好程度
senses.example: We gave the visitors the best possible welcome.
senses.exampleCN: 我们给了来访者尽可能好的接待。
senses.why: When ability is stretched to its limit, possible stops meaning merely can and starts marking the ceiling of what can be reached.
senses.whyCN: 当「能够」被推到极限，possible 就不再只是「可以」，而是标出「能达到的上限」。

intro.en: Possible comes from Latin posse, to be able, whose stem joins an old word for power with the verb to be.
intro.cn: possible 出自拉丁语 posse（能够），其词干由表示「有力量」的古老词与动词「是」组合而成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning powerful or able, usually written *poti-, is generally thought to lie behind the Latin family.
items.cn: 一般认为，表示「有力量、有能力」的重构词根 *poti- 是拉丁这一族词的远祖。

items.en: Latin potis meant able, capable or powerful, and it combined with esse, to be, to build the verb of ability.
items.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为「有能力的、有力量的」，它与 esse（是）结合，构成表示「能够」的动词。

items.en: From posse Latin formed the adjective possibilis, meaning that which can be done or can exist.
items.cn: 拉丁语由 posse 造出形容词 possibilis，意为「做得到的、能够存在的」。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as possible and passed it to English, keeping the sense of what can be or can happen.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 possible 并传入英语，保留了「能够存在或发生」的意思。

items.en: English added -ity for the abstract noun, -ly for the adverb and im- for the negative, so one Latin stem now covers a small family.
items.cn: 英语后来加上 -ity 构成抽象名词、加 -ly 构成副词、加 im- 构成否定式，同一个拉丁词干如今撑起了一个小词族。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same Latin verb of ability; the second collects words that also talk about what may happen.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「能够」词族上的词；近义组收同样谈论「也许会发生」的词。

entries.definition: The adverb built from possible with -ly, meaning perhaps.
entries.definitionCN: 由 possible 加 -ly 构成的副词，意为「也许」。

entries.definition: Not able to happen or be done, formed with the negative prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀 im- 构成，意为「不可能的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the chance that something may exist or happen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事存在或发生的「可能性」的名词。

entries.definition: Powerful or effective, from the same old word for able that feeds posse.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「强有力的」，与 posse 同出表示「有能力」的古老词。

entries.definition: Expected to happen or probably true.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生或大概是真的。

entries.definition: Strongly likely, more confident than merely possible.
entries.definitionCN: 很有可能，语气比 possible 更确定。

entries.definition: Able to be carried out in practice, with the means available.
entries.definitionCN: 在现有条件下能够实际做到的。

entries.definition: Able to be imagined or believed, however unlikely.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被想象或相信的，尽管可能性很小。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of ability, and its family keeps adding endings that turn ability into a noun, an adverb or its opposite.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「能够」的动词上，同族词不断加后缀，把「能力」变成名词、副词或它的反面。

normal.en: Posse in Latin means to be able, so anything possible is something you are able to do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为「能够」，所以 possible 就是「做得到的事」。

normal.en: Potis, the old word for able, also hides inside potent and potential, so power runs through the whole family.
normal.cn: 表示「有能力」的古词 potis 也藏在 potent 与 potential 里，力量贯穿整个词族。

normal.en: Add -ity to possible and the chance itself becomes a noun: possibility.
normal.cn: 在 possible 后加 -ity，机会本身就变成名词 possibility。

normal.en: Add im- to possible and the ability disappears: impossible.
normal.cn: 在 possible 前加 im-，能力就消失，成了 impossible。

normal.en: The phrase as soon as possible keeps the old sense of ability pressed against a deadline.
normal.cn: 短语 as soon as possible 把古老的「能力」之意压到一个截止时间上。

abstract.en: A door that is not locked is possible; whether anyone walks through it is a separate question.
abstract.cn: 门没上锁，这叫 possible；有没有人走进去，是另一回事。

abstract.en: Possible marks the edge of the map rather than a road already travelled.
abstract.cn: possible 标的是地图的边缘，而不是已经走过的路。

abstract.en: Every finished thing was once only possible, which is why the word keeps a hint of the future.
abstract.cn: 每件完成的事当初都只是 possible，所以这个词总带着一点未来的气味。

examples.en: Is it possible to finish the report by Friday?
examples.cn: 有可能在周五前完成报告吗？

examples.en: The doctors did everything possible to save him.
examples.cn: 医生们为救他做了一切能做的事。

examples.en: A peaceful solution is still possible.
examples.cn: 和平解决仍然是有可能的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕谁保」——怕谁保不住，事情就只好说「有可能」；记住 possible 表示可能的。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）← potis（有能力的）+ esse（是）；同族词多与「能力、可能」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ability without obstruction; from there the word spreads to likelihood, to fitness for a purpose, and to the upper limit of what can be reached.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「有能力、无阻碍」；由此分出「可能性大小」「是否合适」，以及「能达到的上限」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door left unlocked, with a path visible behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇没有上锁的门，门后能看见一条路。

branches.en: a locked door that someone finally opens
branches.cn: 一扇终于被人打开的锁着的门

branches.en: a forecast that says rain is likely by evening
branches.cn: 预报说傍晚大概有雨

branches.en: a shortlist with only one suitable name on it
branches.cn: 名单上只剩一个合适的人

branches.en: a welcome pushed to its warmest
branches.cn: 把欢迎做到最热烈

branches.en: a seed that may or may not sprout
branches.cn: 一粒可能发芽也可能不发芽的种子

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of ability, its older root of power, a suffix of possibility, and English endings that reverse or redirect it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「能够」动词、更早的「力量」词根、表示「可……的」后缀，以及英语中表示否定与副词的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse, potis and possibilis supply the core; the English family grows by prefix and suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 posse、potis、possibilis 提供核心，英语这一族靠前缀与后缀继续生长。

definition_zh: 风；风力；气息；风声、消息；趋势；（管乐器中的）管乐；使喘不过气；缠绕（读 /waɪnd/）
definition_en: natural air moving across the earth's surface; also breath, a hint of news, a tendency, or to twist something around
core_image: 整片草叶被同一股力量压向一侧，沙粒贴着地面快速爬行，旗面被撑得笔直
scene: 海边的山坡上，草全部向同一方向倒伏，观察者说 The wind bends the grass flat against the hillside.
sceneCN: 这里 wind 指「在地表流动的自然空气」（第 1 个义项：能推动物体、改变植物形态的风）；句意为风把草压得贴向山坡。图中可辨识物件：倒伏的草、旗子、沙粒、远处的海面。

pos.zh: 风；风力；气息；风声；趋势；管乐器（读 /wɪnd/）
缠绕；上发条；使弯曲前进（同形异音，读 /waɪnd/）

senses.title: Natural air in motion
senses.definition: air moving across the surface of the earth, usually named by the direction it comes from
senses.definitionCN: 沿地表流动的空气，通常按来向命名
senses.example: A warm wind came off the desert at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一阵暖风从沙漠方向吹来。
senses.why: The noun is one of the oldest words in English, and its core is simply air that moves.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是英语最古老的词之一，核心意思不过是「在动的空气」。

senses.title: Force or strength of moving air
senses.definition: the speed or force of the air, often graded on a scale for weather and sailing
senses.definitionCN: 空气的速度或力量，常按天气与航海的分级来衡量
senses.example: The wind reached gale force before the harbour closed.
senses.exampleCN: 港口关闭前，风力已达到大风级。
senses.why: Once wind names the moving air, the same word naturally names how strongly it blows.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 wind 指流动的空气，同一个词自然也能指它吹得有多强。

senses.title: Breath or power to breathe
senses.definition: the ability to breathe easily, especially after effort
senses.definitionCN: 顺畅呼吸的能力，尤指用力之后
senses.example: He stopped at the top of the hill to get his wind back.
senses.exampleCN: 他在山顶停下，好把气缓过来。
senses.why: Breath was thought of as air moving in and out of the body, so the outdoor word was borrowed for the inner one.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸被看作空气在身体里进出，于是户外的词被借去指体内的空气。

senses.title: A hint or rumour
senses.definition: a piece of news or a hint that has begun to spread quietly
senses.definitionCN: 开始悄悄传开的一点消息或暗示
senses.example: The staff got wind of the merger before it was announced.
senses.exampleCN: 员工在合并公布之前就听到了风声。
senses.why: News was imagined as something carried on the air, arriving before any official statement.
senses.whyCN: 消息被想象成随风而来的东西，比正式声明先到。

senses.title: A tendency or force of change
senses.definition: a widespread movement of opinion or events that pushes change in a direction
senses.definitionCN: 推动事情朝某方向改变的普遍舆论或事件趋势
senses.example: The winds of reform reached even the oldest institutions.
senses.exampleCN: 改革之风甚至吹到了最古老的机构。
senses.why: The metaphor makes social change a weather system, with direction and force of its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把社会变化变成天气系统，自带方向与力量。

senses.title: Wind instruments
senses.definition: the group of instruments played by blowing air, such as flutes and trumpets
senses.definitionCN: 靠吹气发声的一组乐器，如长笛与小号
senses.example: The wind section entered after the strings faded.
senses.exampleCN: 弦乐渐弱之后，管乐声部进来了。
senses.why: These instruments work by moving air, so players shorten 'wind instruments' to 'the wind'.
senses.whyCN: 这些乐器靠推动空气发声，因此乐手把 wind instruments 缩称为 the wind。

senses.title: To leave someone breathless
senses.definition: to hit or exhaust someone so that they cannot breathe easily for a moment
senses.definitionCN: 撞击或消耗某人，使其一时无法顺畅呼吸
senses.example: The fall winded him for a full minute.
senses.exampleCN: 那一跤让他足足一分钟喘不上气。
senses.why: The verb reverses the breath sense: instead of having wind, a person has it knocked out.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词反转了气息义：人不是有了气，而是气被打掉了。

senses.title: To twist or coil
senses.definition: to wrap something around an object, or to turn a key or handle to make a mechanism work
senses.definitionCN: 把某物绕在物体上，或转动钥匙、手柄使机械运转
senses.example: She wound the old clock every Sunday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个星期天早上给那座旧钟上发条。
senses.why: This is a different word, pronounced with a long vowel, that happens to share the spelling; its core is turning or coiling.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个词，读长元音，只是拼写相同；其核心义是转动或盘绕。

intro.en: Wind is a native Germanic noun from Old English wind. Its deeper root is reconstructed, and Latin ventus is a genuine cognate from the same source rather than the origin of the English word. The verb meaning 'to twist' is a separate homograph with a long vowel.
intro.cn: wind 是古英语 wind 传承下来的日耳曼本族名词。其更深词根为重构形式；拉丁语 ventus 是同出该源的真实同源词，而非英语词的来源。意为「缠绕」的动词是另一个同形异音词，读长元音。

items.en: Wind meant 'moving air' and was already the everyday noun for weather; the same form also served for breath.
items.cn: wind 意为「流动的空气」，早已是谈天气的日常名词；同一形式也用于指呼吸。

items.en: The noun goes back to a Germanic form reconstructed as *windaz, with relatives in Dutch wind and German Wind.
items.cn: 这个名词上溯到重构的日耳曼形式 *windaz，在荷兰语 wind 与德语 Wind 中有亲属。

items.en: The usual reconstruction is a root meaning 'to blow', written *h₂weh₁-; it is a reconstructed form, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 通常把词根重构为意为「吹」的 *h₂weh₁-；这是重构形式，不是有记录的实际词。

items.en: Latin ventus 'wind' comes from the same deep root, so it is a cognate; English did not borrow the word from it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ventus「风」来自同一深层词根，因此是同源词；英语并非从它借入这个词。

items.en: Breath, rumour, tendency and the musical sense are later extensions; their exact first dates are uncertain and should not be given as fixed facts.
items.cn: 呼吸、风声、趋势与音乐义都是后来的延伸；其确切首见年代不确定，不宜当作固定事实。

note.en: Group one holds words that contain wind but mean something else; group two holds actual wind words that differ in strength or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是含有 wind 字样但意思不同的词；第二组是真正表示风、但力度或场合有别的词。

entries.definition: An opening in a wall for light and air, from Old Norse vindauga 'wind-eye'; it is not a form of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 墙上用于透光和通风的开口，来自古诺尔斯语 vindauga「风眼」；它不是 wind 的词形变化。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'exposed to much wind' or 'long-winded'; it is derived from wind, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「多风的」或「话多的」；由 wind 派生，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: The past participle meaning 'left out of breath', from the verb sense of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，意为「被弄得喘不上气」，来自 wind 的动词义。

entries.definition: The participle of the other wind, pronounced with a long vowel: twisting, or following a twisting path.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个 wind 的分词，读长元音：缠绕的，或沿弯曲路径延伸的。

entries.definition: A light, pleasant wind, often from the sea; wind itself can be any strength.
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔宜人的风，常指海风；wind 则可指任何强度。

entries.definition: A very strong wind, especially one graded on the Beaufort scale; it is a level of wind, not a different phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 极强的风，尤指蒲福风级中的一级；它是风的一个等级，不是另一种现象。

entries.definition: A sudden short blast of wind; it is a momentary event within a steadier wind.
entries.definitionCN: 突然而短促的一阵风；是较稳定风中的瞬时事件。

entries.definition: A current of cool air inside a building; wind is usually the outdoor weather word.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑内部的冷空气流；wind 通常指户外的天气现象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real native root, a real cognate and real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的英语本族词根、真实同源词与真实复合词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English wind; the same Germanic stock gives Dutch wind and German Wind.
normal.cn: 古英语 wind；同日耳曼词源给出荷兰语 wind 与德语 Wind。

normal.en: Latin ventus is a cognate, not the source; the two words grew from the same deep root.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ventus 是同源词而非来源；两个词从同一深层词根长出。

normal.en: Compounds mark the uses: wind speed, windmill, windbreak, windward.
normal.cn: 复合词标出用法：风速、风车、防风林、迎风。

normal.en: The phrase 'get wind of' keeps the old image of news arriving on the air.
normal.cn: 「get wind of」保留了消息随风而来的旧意象。

normal.en: Remember the homograph: the twisting verb is wound and winding, not winded.
normal.cn: 记住同形异音词：缠绕义的过去式是 wound、分词是 winding，不是 winded。

abstract.en: Picture a flag pulling so hard that the pole leans with it.
abstract.cn: 想象旗子拉得那么用力，连旗杆都跟着倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour crossing a playground faster than any child can run.
abstract.cn: 想象一则谣言穿过操场，比任何孩子跑得都快。

abstract.en: Picture an old clock key turning in a slow circle until the spring is tight.
abstract.cn: 想象一把旧钟的发条钥匙慢慢转圈，直到弹簧绷紧。

examples.en: The wind tore the awning loose before the storm arrived.
examples.cn: 风暴到来之前，风把遮阳篷扯松了。

examples.en: She stood still until she had her wind again.
examples.cn: 她站住不动，直到气息恢复。

examples.en: The conductor asked the wind to play softer in the second movement.
examples.cn: 指挥要求管乐在第二乐章吹得更轻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温的」——温的空气一动起来，就成了风

root: 古英语 wind「流动的空气」，属日耳曼语族，可上溯重构形式 *windaz 与意为「吹」的印欧词根 *h₂weh₁-（重构形式）。拉丁语 ventus 为同源词而非来源。意为「缠绕」的动词是同形异音词，读 /waɪnd/，与本条名词不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: air in motion is first weather, then its strength, then the breath inside a body, then news and social change carried on the air, then the instruments that use it, and finally two verbs, one about breath and one about twisting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：运动的空气先是天气，再是它的强度，然后是体内的气息，再是随风传播的消息与社会变化，然后是借空气发声的乐器，最后是两个动词，一个关于气息，一个关于缠绕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grass bent flat in one direction while sand skims the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：草被压得倒向一侧，沙粒贴着地面飞掠。

branches.en: WEATHER: the moving air and the strength with which it blows.
branches.cn: 天气：流动的空气与它吹出的力量。

branches.en: BREATH IN AND OUT: having wind, and having it knocked away.
branches.cn: 气息进出：有气，与气被打掉。

branches.en: AIRBORNE NEWS: rumours and reform both travel like weather.
branches.cn: 随风的消息：谣言与改革都像天气一样传播。

branches.en: BLOWN INSTRUMENTS: music made by moving air through a tube.
branches.cn: 吹奏乐器：让空气穿过管子而发声。

branches.en: THE HOMOGRAPH: a separate verb of turning and coiling, pronounced long.
branches.cn: 同形异音词：另一个表示转动与盘绕的动词，读长元音。

intro.en: Wind is a free native root that takes -y, -less, -ward and joins compounds such as windmill and windbreak; a separate homograph wind 'to twist' adds wound and winding.
intro.cn: wind 是自由的本族词根，可加 -y、-less、-ward，并与 windmill、windbreak 等构成复合词；另有同形异音词 wind「缠绕」，给出 wound 与 winding。

latinIntro.en: Latin ventus 'wind' is a cognate from the same deep root, and ventosus 'windy' belongs to that Latin family; neither is the source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ventus「风」是同出深层词根的同源词，ventosus「多风的」属于该拉丁词族；两者都不是英语词的来源。

items.example: The wind rose with the tide.

items.meaning: to twist, coil or turn a key
items.example: Wind the string around the spool.
The ridge is windy even in summer.
The lake lay windless at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 黎明时湖面一丝风也没有。

items.meaning: on the side the wind blows from
items.example: The windward slope gets more rain.

items.meaningCN: 风力驱动的磨坊或风车

items.meaning: a row of trees or a barrier that blocks wind
items.example: The poplar windbreak protects the orchard.
items.exampleCN: 白杨防风林保护着果园。

items.meaningCN: 受风侵袭的；被风吹得光秃的
items.example: A windswept headland faced the sea.
items.exampleCN: 一片受风的岬角面向大海。

latinEntries.structure: ventus, venti (m., second declension; cognate, not source)

definition_zh: 谈话；说话；讲座；会谈
definition_en: to speak to someone, or a conversation or a speech on a subject
core_image: 两个人在街角站着说话
scene: 两个老朋友在街角站着聊了很久。 The two old friends stood at the corner and talked for a long time.
sceneCN: 这里 talk 是「交谈、说话」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两个老朋友在街角站着聊了很久。

senses.title: To speak with someone
senses.definition: to speak to another person in an informal way
senses.definitionCN: 以轻松的方式对另一个人说话
senses.example: The two old friends talked for a long time.
senses.exampleCN: 两个老朋友聊了很久。
senses.why: The verb comes from the same family as tale and tell, the act of putting words between people.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与 tale、tell 同族，核心是人与人之间交换话语。

senses.title: A lecture on a subject
senses.definition: a speech given to an audience about a topic
senses.definitionCN: 就某个题目对听众所作的演讲
senses.example: She gave a talk on climate change.
senses.exampleCN: 她作了一场关于气候变化的讲座。
senses.why: A talk is one voice speaking at length to many.

senses.whyCN: 谈话一旦正式并且反复进行，就成了外交层面的「会谈」。

intro.en: Talk is a Middle English verb tied to tale and tell.
intro.cn: talk 是中古英语动词，与 tale、tell 同源。

items.en: The root meant to recount or tell.
items.cn: 词根意为讲述、叙说。

items.en: Tale meant a story or account.
items.cn: tale 意为故事或叙述。

items.en: Talken meant to speak or converse.
items.cn: talken 意为说话、交谈。

items.en: Talk covered both chat and formal discussion.
items.cn: talk 兼顾闲聊与正式商谈。

items.en: The noun added lectures and negotiations.
items.cn: 名词义又扩展出讲座与谈判。

note.en: Talk is set beside look-alike words and beside verbs of speaking.
note.cn: 把 talk 与形近词以及表示说话的动词作对比。

normalIntro.en: Talk belongs to the tale-and-tell family, where words pass between people.
normalIntro.cn: talk 属于 tale 与 tell 的词族，话语在人与人之间传递。

normal.en: The two old friends talked for a long time.

abstract.en: Repeated talk hardens into negotiation.

sensesIntro.en: Talk runs from private conversation to public lecture to official negotiation.
sensesIntro.cn: talk 从私下交谈，延伸到公开讲座与正式谈判。

core.cn: 核心意象：两个人在街角交换话语。

branches.cn: 交谈是最日常的分支。

branches.cn: 讲座是对听众的谈话。

branches.cn: 正式谈话变成谈判。

branches.en: Both are voices exchanging meaning.

branches.cn: 公开与正式言说共享同一个舞台。

definition_zh: 表演者；演员；演奏者；执行者；表现良好的人或物
definition_en: a person who acts, sings, dances or plays music for an audience; also a person or thing that carries out a task or reaches a particular level of results
core_image: 一束光落在舞台中央，一个人抬脚走进去，把练了千百遍的动作交给台下
scene: 演出开始前，幕布后面很安静，只有鞋底轻轻碰着地板的声音。 The performer walked to the centre of the stage and the hall went quiet.
sceneCN: 这里是「表演者、演员」（第 1 个义项：为观众表演的人）；句意为表演者走到舞台中央，整个大厅随即安静下来。

pos.zh: 表演者；演员；演奏者；执行者；表现良好的人或物

derivatives.zh: 来自古法语 parfournir，义为「表演；执行；运转」
perform 加名词后缀 -ance，义为「表演；表现；性能」
perform 加 -ing 作形容词，义为「表演的；执行的」，如表演艺术
perform 加 -ative，义为「述行性的；与表演有关的」

senses.title: Someone who entertains an audience
senses.definition: a person who acts, sings, dances or plays music in front of an audience
senses.definitionCN: 在观众面前演戏、唱歌、跳舞或演奏音乐的人
senses.example: The performer held the audience for two hours without a break.
senses.exampleCN: 这位表演者让观众连着看了两个小时，中间没有休息。
senses.why: Perform first meant to carry a task through to the end; when the task is a song or a role done in public, the one who carries it out becomes the performer.
senses.whyCN: perform 最初指把事情做到最后；当被做到最后的东西是一支歌或一个角色，而且是在众人面前完成时，完成它的人就成了表演者。

senses.title: Someone who carries out a task
senses.definition: a person who does a piece of work or a duty, especially one that is hard or needs skill
senses.definitionCN: 完成某项工作或职责的人，尤指任务艰难或需要技巧时
senses.example: She is the quiet performer who finishes whatever the team plans.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那个不声不响的执行者，团队计划的事都由她做完。
senses.why: The stage sense grew out of the older sense of finishing a job, so the word still names anyone who actually gets the work done, even with no audience at all.
senses.whyCN: 舞台义是从「把活干完」这个更早的意思长出来的，所以这个词仍指真正把事情做完的人，哪怕台下根本没有观众。

senses.title: A person or thing that delivers results
senses.definition: a person, company or product that reaches a particular level of success or efficiency
senses.definitionCN: 达到某种成功程度或效率的人、公司或产品
senses.example: Reviewers called the small car a solid performer on long drives.
senses.exampleCN: 评测者称这款小车在长途行驶中表现可靠。
senses.why: Once performer names whoever completes an action, business writing extends it to anything judged by how well it acts, so a car or a company can be a good performer too.
senses.whyCN: 既然 performer 指把动作完成的人，商业语境就把它扩展到一切按「做得怎么样」来评价的对象，于是汽车或公司也能被称为表现良好者。

intro.en: Performer is the English verb perform plus the suffix -er; the verb itself came through Old French from a Frankish stem, with a Latin prefix at its head.
intro.cn: performer 是英语动词 perform 加后缀 -er 构成；动词本身经古法语来自法兰克语词干，词首则是一个拉丁语前缀。

items.en: The Latin prefix per- meant through or thoroughly, and it survives in the first syllable of the English verb.
items.cn: 拉丁语前缀 per- 意为「穿过、彻底」，保存在这个英语动词的第一个音节里。

items.en: The second element is usually traced to a reconstructed Frankish verb meaning to provide or accomplish; because the form is reconstructed, the source is not fully certain.
items.cn: 第二部分一般追溯到重构的法兰克语动词，意为「提供、完成」；由于该形式是重构的，来源并不完全确定。

items.en: Old French parfournir meant to complete or carry out fully, joining par- with fournir.
items.cn: 古法语 parfournir 意为「彻底完成、履行」，由 par- 与 fournir 组合而成。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as performen, first meaning to accomplish a task and later to act a role or play music.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 performen，先指完成任务，后来才指扮演角色或演奏音乐。

items.en: The suffix -er was added to name the person, and by the sixteenth century performer covered both stage artists and people who carry out duties.
items.cn: 加上后缀 -er 用来指人，到十六世纪 performer 已同时指舞台艺人与履行职责的人。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same verb; the near-meaning group collects the kinds of people who stand in front of an audience.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一动词上的词；近义组收各类站在观众面前的人。

entries.definition: To carry out an action, or to act, sing or play for an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 执行某项行动；也指为观众表演、演唱或演奏。

entries.definition: The act of performing, or how well someone or something does.
entries.definitionCN: 表演这一行为；也指某人或某物的表现。

entries.definition: The adjective describing arts or actions that are performed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容需要当众表演的艺术或动作。

entries.definition: Relating to language or behaviour that does something by being said or done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容言语或行为本身即在完成某事的；述行性的。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to amuse an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 以娱乐观众为职业的人。

entries.definition: A person who creates or performs art.
entries.definitionCN: 从事艺术创作或表演的人。

entries.definition: A person who performs a role in a play or film.
entries.definitionCN: 在戏剧或电影中扮演角色的人。

entries.definition: A person who plays or writes music.
entries.definitionCN: 演奏或创作音乐的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is the verb plus the person suffix, and the verb still carries the older idea of finishing what was started.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是动词加「做某事的人」后缀，而动词本身仍带着「把开始的事做完」这个更早的意思。

normal.en: Perform plus -er makes the doer: the person who performs.
normal.cn: perform 加 -er 造出动作的执行者，也就是表演的人。

normal.en: The -er here works exactly as in singer, dancer and teacher.
normal.cn: 这里的 -er 与 singer、dancer、teacher 里的 -er 作用完全相同。

normal.en: Perform came from Old French parfournir, to carry out fully, and only later took the stage sense.
normal.cn: perform 来自古法语 parfournir，意为彻底完成，舞台义是后来才有的。

normal.en: Performance is the act, performer is the person: the pair fills two slots of the same event.
normal.cn: performance 指行为，performer 指人，两者正好填满同一件事的两个位置。

normal.en: A good performer in a business report means a product that sells well, not a singer.
normal.cn: 商业报告里的 good performer 指卖得好的产品，不是歌手。

abstract.en: Think of the moment a person crosses from the dark wings into the light: that single step makes an ordinary person a performer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人从昏暗的侧幕走进灯光的那一瞬间，这一步就把普通人变成了表演者。

abstract.en: Any job done in public turns the worker into a performer, which is why the word slides so easily into business talk.
abstract.cn: 任何在众人面前完成的活都会让干活的人带上表演性质，这就是这个词能轻易滑进商业用语的原因。

abstract.en: The word pairs a finished action with a human body, so it always asks two questions: what was done, and who did it.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个完成的动作和一具人的身体绑在一起，所以它总在问两件事：做了什么，以及谁做的。

examples.en: The performer bowed twice before leaving the stage.
examples.cn: 这位表演者鞠了两次躬才离开舞台。

examples.en: A good performer listens to the room as much as to the script.
examples.cn: 好的表演者听台下的反应，和听台词一样认真。

examples.en: The new engine is a strong performer in cold weather.
examples.cn: 这款新发动机在低温下表现强劲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼佛么」——他一开口就把情绪泼满全场，观众直问这是哪来的佛么；记住 performer 是表演者。

root: 英语动词 perform 加后缀 -er 构成；perform 一般认为来自古法语 parfournir（彻底完成），词首 per- 来自拉丁语，词干 fournir 源自法兰克语，来源不完全确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is someone who carries an action through; the senses then split between the stage, the workplace and any object judged by results.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把某个动作完成到底的人；义项由此分为舞台上的表演者、工作中的执行者，以及任何按表现好坏来评价的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single figure stepping out of the wings into a pool of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人从侧幕走出，踏进一小片灯光里。

branches.en: a singer bowing under a single spotlight
branches.cn: 聚光灯下鞠躬的歌手

branches.en: a dancer counting the beat in the wings
branches.cn: 侧幕里数着节拍的舞者

branches.en: a clerk who finishes every item on the list
branches.cn: 把清单每一项都做完的职员

branches.en: a company praised for strong quarterly numbers
branches.cn: 因季度业绩亮眼而受称赞的公司

branches.en: a machine that does its job and does it well
branches.cn: 既完成任务又完成得漂亮的机器

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix plus a Frankish stem, passed through French, then closed with an English suffix that names the person.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语前缀加法兰克语词干，经法语传来，最后加一个指人的英语后缀收尾。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix per- is Latin; the verb stem reached English from Frankish through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前缀 per- 属于拉丁语；动词词干是经古法语从法兰克语进入英语的。

items.meaning: to carry out; to act or play for an audience
